<div class="pd-leaves">
<section class="pd-desk"></section>
<div class="pd-leaf pd-shelves" hidden><div class="pd-words"><div class="pd-chapter pd-canonical pa-page"><a href="/dougs-library/#the-shelves" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-shelves" class="pd-sentence pd-title pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-referent">The Shelves</div></a><div class="pd-section"><a href="#what-is-here" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="what-is-here" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">What is here</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">Three books are filed under this one. <a href="/dougs-story/" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">Dougs Story</span></a> is mine, and the one book here that is by its own subject. It is the place to begin from, and it begins with <a href="/dougs-story/#starting-over" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">starting over</span></a>. The design of this library is kept in <a href="/dougs-design/" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">Dougs Design</span></a>. The parts I build this library with are in <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">Dougs Reference Manual</span></a>, each beside the chapter that says what it is.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">Each of the three has a chapter here that represents it and carries its synopsis: its entry, drawn on the shelf as a cover with one line under it. In the contents the name opens the entry on this page, and the arrow after it leads to the book itself. And this catalogue is on its own shelf, first, because it is filed under what it is about, which is itself.</div></div><div class="pd-paragraph pd-turn"><a href="/dougs-library/#the-shelves" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-before">← <!-- -->The Shelves</span></a><span class="pd-word pd-count">1 of 5</span><a href="/dougs-library/#the-catalogue" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-after">The Catalogue<!-- --> →</span></a></div></div></div><div class="pd-files"></div></div>
<div class="pd-leaf pd-built"><div class="pd-words"><div class="pd-chapter pd-canonical pa-page"><a href="/dougs-library/#the-catalogue" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-catalogue" class="pd-sentence pd-title pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-referent">The Catalogue</div></a><div class="pd-section"><a href="#how-this-book-is-laid-out" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="how-this-book-is-laid-out" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">How this book is laid out</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">This book is the way into every other, so it is laid out as a place to choose from. It stands in the frame every book of mine stands in, drawn by <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-book" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the base book</span></a>: the library&#x27;s bar black across the top, with my three books as its subjects, each beside a dot in its colour and the open one lit by a line in that colour; this book&#x27;s contents down the opal side bar; and the page beside. It has no head of its own, because its cover stands on its shelf. The page is always the synopsis and the shelf, and under the shelf the entry that is open, if one is. It wears the dark tone, the library&#x27;s own, which is <a href="/dougs-design/#a-black-top-bar-and-an-opal-side-bar" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the black top bar over the opal side bar</span></a>.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">The design it follows is <a href="/dougs-design/#the-shelf" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the shelf</span></a> inside that frame, explored again as <a href="/dougs-design/#the-librarys-page-in-the-frame-of-15" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the library&#x27;s page</span></a>: the covers at two by three in each book&#x27;s colour, with the spine&#x27;s lines and the rule across, six to a row at a desk and three on a phone, and one line under each. Beside this chapter the library&#x27;s subjects are written once, as three references to the books, each saying its book&#x27;s colour, and every book draws them in its bar.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#what-is-on-the-shelf" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="what-is-on-the-shelf" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">What is on the shelf</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The first book on the shelf is this one. The catalogue is filed under what it is about, which is itself, so its own cover stands first, in the site&#x27;s blue-black, and pressing it brings this page back: I was just reading about the thing I am on. That is the closure this library has, shown rather than avoided.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">After it stand the chapters that each represent a book. The class of this book finds them by what they are: a chapter that carries the synopsis of a book other than this one. Its specification says every chapter I add has a place. On the shelf such a chapter is drawn as its book: the title as a cover, and under it one line, the sentence the entry says is <a href="/dougs-library/#the-catalogue" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">its caption</span></a>. The rest of the entry — the book&#x27;s own synopsis — is read when the entry is open.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">An entry opens from its row in the contents, which is marked with the book&#x27;s colour, or from its cover. It opens in place: the volume spans the row under the shelf, the cover large, the caption over the synopsis, as a concept opens in the design book. The title leads to the book. Anywhere else a title refers to its own chapter; in this book, where the chapter carries another book&#x27;s synopsis, it refers to that book, by a class of the framework&#x27;s reference from a title to itself, registered on this book&#x27;s class, so no chapter has to ask for it. The row&#x27;s second word, an arrow, leads to the book too, and is the reference the library requires a catalogue&#x27;s table to carry for every book filed under it.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">The shelf is one view of those chapters, and the views I chose for this book are three: the shelf, the sources and the wall. A view is a thing said of the book, and only one is said at a time, because a view that is said takes the one said before it away. That is how the framework keeps a book to one theme, done here for views. The class says the shelf; the other two are not drawn yet.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#how-it-is-dressed" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="how-it-is-dressed" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">How it is dressed</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The theme is the base&#x27;s with this book&#x27;s scheme, which is the site&#x27;s own — the sea as its colour, the deep blue as its accent, the opal as its side bar — and two parts of its own: the front, which sets the synopsis plain in the serif at the file&#x27;s size, and the covers. Each entry says <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-colour" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">its book&#x27;s colour</span></a>, and the cover on the shelf, the dot in the contents and the dot in the library&#x27;s bar are painted from that one saying. The cover and the table of contents are the framework&#x27;s own, undressed; what they look like here is the base&#x27;s.</div></div><div class="pd-paragraph pd-turn"><a href="/dougs-library/#the-shelves" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-before">← <!-- -->The Shelves</span></a><span class="pd-word pd-count">2 of 5</span><a href="/dougs-story/" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-after">Dougs Story<!-- --> →</span></a></div></div></div><div class="pd-files"><div class="pd-paragraph pd-listing"><span class="pd-word">code.tsx</span><pre class="pd-letter pd-figure pd-code"><code><span class="pd-code-line" data-line="1"><span>import</span> { <span>ReactNode</span> } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;react&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="2"><span>import</span> { $ } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;@dna-platform/chemistry&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="3"><span>import</span> { $Chapter, $Referent, $Synopsis, <span>Self</span> } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;@dna-platform/public&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="4"><span>import</span> { $LibraryBook } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;../.manual/.book&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="5"><span>import</span> { <span>BookLink</span> } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;./o1-the-catalogue~booklink.tsx&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="6"><span>import</span> { <span>Shelf</span> <span>as</span> shelf } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;./o1-the-catalogue~views.tsx&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="7"></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="8"><span>export</span> <span>class</span> <span>$Catalogue</span> <span>extends</span> <span>$LibraryBook</span> {</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="9">    <span>get</span> <span>books</span>(): $Chapter[] {</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="10">        <span>return</span> <span>this</span>.<span>text</span>.<span>find</span>($Chapter).<span>filter</span>(<span><span>chapter</span> =&gt;</span> chapter.<span>is</span>($Synopsis) &amp;&amp; chapter !== <span>this</span>.<span>synopsis</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="11">    }</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="12">    <span>override</span> <span>get</span> <span>placed</span>(): ($Chapter | <span>undefined</span>)[] {</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="13">        <span>return</span> [...<span>super</span>.<span>placed</span>, ...<span>this</span>.<span>books</span>];</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="14">    }</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="15">    <span>override</span> <span>get</span> <span>pages</span>(): $Chapter[] {</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="16">        <span>return</span> [...<span>this</span>.<span>chapters</span>, ...<span>this</span>.<span>books</span>];</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="17">    }</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="18"></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="19">    <span>override</span> <span>head</span>(): <span>ReactNode</span> {</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="20">        <span>return</span> (</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="21">            <span><span>&lt;<span>div</span> <span>className</span>=<span>&quot;pd-switches&quot;</span>&gt;</span></span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="22"><span>                {this.switches()}</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="23"><span>            <span>&lt;/<span>div</span>&gt;</span></span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="24">        );</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="25">    }</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="26"></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="27">    <span>override</span> <span>front</span>(): <span>ReactNode</span> {</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="28">        <span>return</span> (</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="29">            <span><span>&lt;<span>div</span> <span>className</span>=<span>&quot;pd-leaf pd-front pd-open&quot;</span>&gt;</span></span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="30"><span>                {this.opening()}</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="31"><span>            <span>&lt;/<span>div</span>&gt;</span></span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="32">        );</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="33">    }</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="34"></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="35">    <span>override</span> <span>opening</span>(): <span>ReactNode</span> {</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="36">        <span>return</span> (</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="37">            <span><span>&lt;&gt;</span></span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="38"><span>                {super.opening()}</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="39"><span>                <span>&lt;<span>div</span> <span>className</span>=<span>&quot;pd-shelf&quot;</span>&gt;</span></span></span>

        '/dougs-reference-manual/': { key: 'manual', author: 'Doug', art: '<svg viewBox="0 0 64 64" class="pd-illustration"><circle class="pa-fill" cx="24" cy="41" r="10"/><circle class="pa-light" cx="24" cy="41" r="3.5"/><circle cx="24" cy="41" r="3.5"/><path d="M24 28v-4M24 54v4M11 41H7M37 41h4M15 32l-3-3M33 32l3-3M15 50l-3 3M33 50l3 3"/><path class="pa-fill" d="M38 10l5-5 9 9-5 5-4-1L31 30l-5-5 12-12z"/><path d="M38 10l5-5 9 9-5 5-4-1L31 30l-5-5 12-12zM44 12l3 3"/></svg>' },
    };
    // each volume on the shelf: its book, its cover's parts, its name under it
    for (const volume of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-volume')) {
        const link = volume.querySelector('.pd-chapter > a');
        const book = books[link.getAttribute('href')];
        if (!book) continue;
        volume.classList.add(book.key);
        const title = volume.querySelector('.pd-title');
        const name = title.textContent;
        title.innerHTML = '<span class="pa-name">' + name + '</span>' + book.art.replace('class="pd-illustration"', 'id="' + book.key + '-illustration" class="pd-illustration"') + '<span class="pa-author">' + book.author + '</span>';
        const under = document.createElement('div');
        under.className = 'pd-paragraph pa-name-under';
        under.textContent = name;
        volume.appendChild(under);
        // pressing a cover opens the book above the shelf; the shelf stays as it is
        link.addEventListener('click', event => { event.preventDefault(); open(volume, book, name, link.getAttribute('href')); });
    }
    for (const paragraph of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-subjects .pd-paragraph')) {
        const book = books[paragraph.querySelector('a')?.getAttribute('href')];
        if (book) paragraph.classList.add(book.key);
    }
    for (const row of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pa-entry')) {
        const href = row.querySelector('a')?.getAttribute('href') ?? '';
        const book = Object.entries(books).find(([address]) => href.endsWith('#' + address.replaceAll('/', '')))?.[1];
        if (book) { row.classList.add(book.key); row.addEventListener('click', event => { event.preventDefault(); const volume = document.querySelector('.pd-volume.' + book.key); open(volume, book, volume.querySelector('.pa-name').textContent, Object.keys(books).find(a => books[a] === book)); }); }
    }
    for (const glyph of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pa-entry .pa-content'))
        if (glyph.textContent.trim() === '→') glyph.textContent = '▷';
    // the two states: the heading of the contents is the way back to reading, the heading of how it is built the way into the built view
    const view = (state) => { document.body.dataset.view = state; window.scrollTo({ top: 0 }); };
    for (const section of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pd-section')) {
        const heading = section.querySelector(':scope > a:first-child');
        if (!heading) continue;
        heading.addEventListener('click', event => { event.preventDefault(); view(section.classList.contains('pa-appendix') ? 'built' : 'reading'); });
    }
    for (const row of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pd-section.pa-appendix .pa-entry'))
        row.addEventListener('click', event => { event.preventDefault(); view('built'); for (const other of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pa-entry')) other.classList.toggle('pa-open', other === row); });
    document.body.dataset.view = 'reading';
    // the marks at the bar's ends are the two books' covers, cropped to their illustrations
    const marks = {
        library: '<svg class="pd-mark" viewBox="0 0 27 27"><rect class="pa-ground" width="27" height="27"/><rect class="pa-ink" x="0" y="22" width="27" height="2.2"/><rect class="pa-ink" x="2" y="4" width="4" height="18"/><rect class="pa-ink" x="7" y="1" width="3.2" height="21"/><rect class="pa-ink" x="11.2" y="6" width="5" height="16"/><rect class="pa-ink" x="17.2" y="2.5" width="3.4" height="19.5"/><path class="pa-ink" d="M21.6 22 24.2 3.4l2.6.4L24.2 22z"/><rect class="pa-paper" x="3.2" y="8" width="1.6" height="1.6"/><rect class="pa-paper" x="12.4" y="10" width="2.6" height="1.6"/></svg>',
        author: '<svg class="pd-mark" viewBox="0 0 27 27"><rect class="pa-ground" width="27" height="27"/><rect class="pa-paper" x="8" y="-2" width="24" height="26" rx=".8"/><rect class="pa-ink" x="12" y="4" width="11" height="1.4"/><rect class="pa-ink" x="12" y="8" width="11" height="1.4"/><rect class="pa-ink" x="12" y="12" width="7" height="1.4"/><path class="pa-ink" d="M2 25.5 18.5 9l2.6 2.6L4.6 28.1 1 28.6z"/></svg>',
    };
    // a mark is a window cut from its book's illustration, at the scale the illustration has on the open cover
    // a mark refers to the drawing on its book's cover: one drawing on the page, the mark a window onto it
    const clip = (key) => '<span class="pd-mark ' + key + '"><svg class="pd-illustration" viewBox="0 0 64 64"><use href="#' + key + '-illustration"/></svg></span>';
    document.querySelector('.pd-logo .pd-paragraph').insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', clip('library'));
    // the subject the cover is filed under, as its mark; on hover, the subject's name, which is what a press shows
    document.querySelector('.pd-logo').insertAdjacentHTML('beforebegin', '<div class="pd-filed"><div class="pd-paragraph pd-filed-under"><span class="pd-word pa-label">filed under</span><a href="/dougs-library/" class="pa-reference pd-container">' + clip('library') + '</a><span class="pd-word"><a href="/dougs-library/" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">Library</span></a></span></div></div>');
    document.querySelector('.pd-me .pd-byline').insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', clip('story'));
    // The Shelves is this view: its row opens the catalogue's own book on the desk and lights while it is there
    const shelvesRow = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pa-entry')).find(row => row.textContent.includes('The Shelves'));
    if (shelvesRow) { shelvesRow.classList.add('library'); shelvesRow.querySelector('.pa-content').textContent = 'Dougs Library'; shelvesRow.addEventListener('click', event => { event.preventDefault(); const volume = document.querySelector('.pd-volume.library'); open(volume, books['/dougs-library/'], 'Dougs Library', '/dougs-library/'); }); }
    const stage = document.querySelector('.pd-desk');
    const catalogue = document.querySelector('.pd-volume.library');
    const synopsis = document.querySelector('.pd-front .pd-words .pd-paragraph');
    if (catalogue && synopsis) {
        catalogue.appendChild(synopsis.cloneNode(true));
        for (const paragraph of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-shelves .pd-words .pd-paragraph:not(.pd-turn)')) catalogue.appendChild(paragraph.cloneNode(true));
        open(catalogue, books['/dougs-library/'], 'Dougs Library', '/dougs-library/');
    }
    function open(volume, book, name, address) {
        view('reading');
        stage.className = 'pd-desk pa-open ' + book.key;
        const words = Array.from(volume.querySelectorAll('.pd-paragraph:not(.pa-name-under)')).map(p => p.outerHTML).join('');
        stage.innerHTML = '<a class="pa-close" title="close">×</a>' + volume.querySelector('.pd-title').outerHTML.replace(/ id="[a-z]+-illustration"/u, '')
            + '<div class="pd-words"><div class="pa-kicker">filed here</div><h2>' + name + '</h2><div class="pa-line">by <a href="/dougs-story/">' + book.author + '</a> · filed under <a href="/dougs-library/">Library</a></div>' + words
            + '<a class="pa-read" href="' + address + '">Read ' + name + ' →</a></div>';
        stage.querySelector('.pa-close').addEventListener('click', () => {
            stage.className = 'pd-desk'; stage.innerHTML = ''; document.body.dataset.read = 'off';
            for (const row of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pa-entry')) row.classList.remove('pa-open');
        });
        // the words as tall as the cover: when they run past it, they fade and a mark offers to read on
        const column = stage.querySelector('.pd-words');
        column.insertAdjacentHTML('afterend', '<a class="pa-on">' + (document.body.dataset.read === 'on' ? 'the shelf' : 'read on') + '</a>');
        requestAnimationFrame(() => column.classList.toggle('pa-more', column.scrollHeight > column.clientHeight + 4));
        stage.querySelector('.pa-on').addEventListener('click', () => {
            const on = document.body.dataset.read !== 'on';
            document.body.dataset.read = on ? 'on' : 'off';
            stage.querySelector('.pa-on').textContent = on ? 'the shelf' : 'read on';
            requestAnimationFrame(() => column.classList.toggle('pa-more', !on && column.scrollHeight > column.clientHeight + 4));
        });
        for (const row of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pa-entry')) row.classList.toggle('pa-open', row.classList.contains(book.key));
        stage.querySelector('.pa-kicker').textContent = book.key === 'library' ? 'filed under itself' : 'filed here';
        window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' });
        stage.querySelector('.pa-read').textContent = (book.key === 'library' ? 'This is the catalogue: ' : 'Read ') + name + ' →';
    }
</script>
</body>
</html>
The Manual's Page
What I come to the manual for
The reference manual is the book I build the library with: one chapter to a part, the code that is the part beside the chapter that says what it is and how it is used. I come to its page to find a part, read what it is, and read its code without leaving the words — or to read the code first and the words beside it, which is the other way round. So the page is a chapter and its files, read two ways: words forward, where the chapter is the page and its files stand by; and code forward, where the file is the page and the chapter is a brief beside it. I decided that in the sketch phase — the manual read two ways — and the switch between them is a thing said of the book, already built; what the page decides is how each reading looks and how one becomes the other.
The page beside this chapter is the manual's own print — every chapter, every brief, every file, the framework's names on every element — made by The Print and opened from the file. It begins as the manual looks today, set in the frame that The Bookshelf decided: the bar is the cover, with the library's mark as the subject I am filed under, my mark and my name, and my author; the contents stand down the side. From there it is changed one thing at a time, and what I decide is written here in my words, as it was for the bookshelf.
What I decided on the page, in order
The two marks stand next to each other, almost like characters, a small space between; resting on the subject's mark shows the logo of the page a press will go to — the library's mark alone and its name in its ink — with a transition worth watching. The form is utilitarian, a code documentation platform's: the words run wide, the index is a file tree with collapsible levels and marks that help a reader understand, tight enough to scale to a codebase, and the fonts blend the bookshelf's into it — the serif where the library's identity lives, the sans where the manual works. Clicking the code expands it; most of a desk's screen was wasted, so the code and the words now share it.
The transitions of colour, subtle; the moments of drop shadow, pulled back; little moments of nuance at the edge of perception, while the highest-level percept stays elegant and ordinary, the magic a slight feeling. The near-white bars relate differently on different sides of the page, and that stays. The code shows its black on the right; a press docks it as a tab left against the side bar, as in an editor, and if the words are anywhere they are on the right. Three states, and one toggle is the affordance each time, with a hint of the thing it expands. Syntax highlighting for as many languages as possible, and options for how code is viewed.
Every piece of code has a mark that grounds it in a design and a colour: one of seven sorts, each a shape and a colour, so related code looks related, with a key. The marks have the same square feel as the site's, as if of a type — a statement about what it means for something to have a visual representation — slightly utilitarian, somewhat abstract, always at the left. The mark belongs to the chapter as well as to its files. The groups of the contents no longer read as sentences foreign to a tree: a folder's mark and its own words.
The page, built
The manual on 4242 the same day, carried from this page in the order the page's own script does things, each piece measured as it landed. The bar first, as every book's: a cover holds the cover of the book it is filed under, and the base book draws the logo from the two, the subject's mark, the book's own mark and the two names, one waiting under the other; it is in The Cover, and the catalogue gave back what it had drawn alone. Then the index as a tree: a folder is said of each section of the table by the manual at bind, its layer drawing the chevron and the folder's mark before the heading; a chevron is a switch whose press folds the section or the chapter's row it stands on, and the key is said folded in the table itself; a chapter's files stand beneath it as presses, each a file, which opens the chapter and the file in the split. All of that is in The Entry and The Listing.
The page's three states are the manual's three readings, words forward, split and code forward, annotations of one family on the book that a press switches, and the spread lays the page as a grid in each: the words wide with the rail at the edge; the words beside the panel with the editor's tab bar at its head, the file's tabs, the words tab, the dock and the options; and the panel across the page with the grip at the edge. The open file is the book's, named by whichever press chose it, and the opened listing wears it. The options, light code, wrapping and line numbers, are three more things said of the book, each a switch. It is all in The Manual, the type of book another subject's manual extends in one line.
What the port found, measured, and changed. A hover written as a state on the logo blocked the page for 1,794 milliseconds, because a child's state redraws the whole book and the book's redraw re-walked every chapter for every entry and icon; the book now indexes its places once at bind, the redraw is 767 milliseconds, the same as any press, and the hover is a field on the logo, written true when the pointer enters the subject's mark and false when it leaves the logo, by handlers the logo says in its container, and said as a class by an annotation, so the subject stays unfolded while the pointer crosses to its name and the name is its link, with nothing in the logo that is React's. A press that compared what an earlier press had put into the book with the reading it had imported worked once and then never, because the imported component is a factory and the component a press passes is the instance's own, one object per instance; so every press in the manual is a noun that compares what came through its props with what came through its props, as the tab always did, and the rule is written down. Then the audit, on my word that the marks were pressed together and the gradients and the nuance were missing: one probe read the same forty properties on this page and on the built manual, and every difference had a cause in the sheet, a rule of the port losing to a base rule that came later or bound tighter, a selector naming the wrong sibling, the wash on the page's body and on nothing of the book; mended, the bar, the side bar and the words measure as the page's. And the fold's slowness, profiled: a press on a folder's chevron makes the whole book render again from its root, three seconds in the dev serve and three quarters of one in the build, most of it React and the framework redrawing what did not change and the code figure highlighting every file again. That is a finding about the framework, written up for the pitch list, not something the page can fix, and the framework fixed it the next day; what that uncovered is under the switch, below. The names changed with the port: the marks and the name in the bar are the logo, since a masthead is a part of a boat. What is not carried: the presses for a chapter's files under its title, which wait on a face for the title. The chapters themselves did not change beyond the one line that keys them.
The key, built
The marks were the first thing carried from the page into the manual, the same day, on my word that there might be a pattern for them: a resource file in the appendix that a chapter imports as a reference. There is, and it is the cover's pattern turned on the key's entries. The page's seven glyphs and its lookup from a chapter's name to its entry became an appendix section of the manual's table, the key, with one chapter per entry holding its drawing and its colour, and each chapter keyed to its entry by a reference. It is built in The Key, with the code beside that chapter, and the entries are its seven neighbours, from A Type of Book to A Tool; how a new chapter or a new entry joins is said there, under how the key scales.
An entry opened: the drawing large under its title, and the words for what the entry is. The rest of the page, the tree with its chevrons, the rail and the split, the file's thin-line icon and the colour on a file's press, is carried under the page, built, above, and what the carrying uncovered is under the switch, built, below; this chapter is where the team reads what was decided and follows a mention to where it is built.
The switch, built
The day after the key, the framework under the library changed: a piece of writing now draws when its own state, its props, its theme or something it read while drawing changed, and otherwise answers what it drew last. The fold that took three seconds in the dev serve fell to a fifth of one, and every switch, tab, chevron and file press in the manual stopped reading its pressed state. The reason was the container. A piece of writing chooses the element it draws through inside its own draw and hands it an id, its classes and its children; React then calls that element after the draw, with nothing watching, so an element that reads at draw time reads something no one will answer. The switch's button had read the book's annotations through its pressed attribute, and it had looked alive only because every write redrew the whole book. What we had been relying on was the cascade.
The seam that fixes it is one method on every piece of writing, its container, which draws the element with what the view hands it, and which a subclass overrides to say its own attributes, typed by the browser's own, and hand the rest through: a switch says it is a button with a click; a chevron says a click that leaves the link under it alone; a file's press says its colour. The element had been the only place an attribute could be said, so every subclass that needed one had made a component of its own and read outside the draw; now none does. It is built in The Switch, and the chevrons and the file presses that use it are in The Entry and The Listing.
Two things found on the way. The folders in the manual's tree had stopped folding, and that was the theme, not the framework: the row rule that says the book first, from the audit, weighed the same as the fold's rule and came later in the sheet, so the fold's rules say the book first too. And the logo's hover was a hook of React's, which this library does not use; it is a field on the logo now, written by the logo's own methods from the handlers its container says, and said as a class by an annotation, so the subject stays unfolded while the pointer crosses to its name. That is in The Cover. What was tried and refused on the way is kept where the team reads: an off switch for the framework's memory, a lift of the button into a draw of its own, a hover held by the sheet alone, which cannot remember, and a second note before a text, which would have walked the annotations twice.
What a press costs now, measured like with like: one task of about seven tenths of a second on a page of twenty thousand nodes, the same for a tab, an option, a fold and the hover, and the profile leads with the framework's own readings of the open chapter, each a walk of the book re-run by every row that read it. That is the next thing, and it belongs to the framework.
The part, built
The manual's page in the catalogue, the day after the manual's own. I wanted an appendix that might be, or have elements of, a reference manual, since almost every book ends up with an appendix for the components used to make it, almost like the genome of the book. What came of it is two things in the reference manual, a part and a view. A part is a grouping of chapters and nothing more: a chapter says which part it is in at its head, with the part's name as its words, and the table of contents answers the grouping. It requires no place, no anchor and no form in the table, and the table is written however I write it; the part is the framework's now, and I decided that the implementer is free to integrate parts as they like, with headings in their table or without. How a part's chapters are shown is a view, a format said of each of them, and the manual is the one view this library has, the same code the reference manual itself is built on, so there is one way to write a reference manual and the catalogue's chapter on how it is built says two lines at its head and is read as the manual reads a chapter: beside its file, in the catalogue's own colours, with the tree for its part down the side, the shelf and the desk stepping aside while it is open. The folder in the tree is the part's place in the page, and its mark is a press to the part's first chapter, which is where a part is reached, as a book is reached through its cover. It is all in The Part and The Manual, with the tree's own piece in The Entry and what the base does for every book in The Book.
The same two lines in this book's six chapters on how it is built and in my story's one, and each book keeps its own tone: the design book's cobalt bar and rose over the tree, the story's serif on its paper with the files in the dark panel at the right. Nothing in the reference manual changed in function, performance or style, which was the condition I set: measured on the bound site, every one of a hundred and forty-four computed properties on its page the same as before, its three states by their columns the same, its folders folding to the same heights, and its seven presses between 463 and 759 milliseconds against the 635 to 718 before. What the carrying taught is in the chapters: a part's heading in the table wears an id as every heading does, so a part is named so that no chapter's title wears the same one; a view's rules stand earlier in the sheet than a theme's, so each says the book first and its own class; and the framework assumes nothing about which chapters are in parts, since a chapter answers its part or none and whatever reads parts filters by checking, so the chapters of this book that are not its appendix say no part at all.
And the other way round, a second reference manual, made to prove the abstraction holds in both cases and not only in the one it was carried from. A galley of this library was pulled aside and a manual of my story's two parts, the sheet and the papers, written into it as an author would write it: a book whose class extends the manual's in one line, a cover, a synopsis and a table as any book here has, each of its two chapters saying it is a manual and opening with a brief, its code beside it, a chapter and a row in the catalogue. Bound, it is this page in every part, the bar, the tree with its folder and its numbered rows and file presses, the brief, the turn and the rail, and the catalogue shelves it as a fifth jacket. The galley was then thrown away; what it proved stays here.
How a manual is made
This is the page I come back to when I want a manual, or an appendix read as one, because the same six things make every case. A part is a grouping of chapters, the framework's, and a chapter says which part it is in at its head: The Part. The manual is a format said of a chapter, the one way a part is read here: a chapter beside its files read three ways, its row in the tree given its presses, and a class on the book while one of its chapters is open: The Manual. A folder is the tree's own piece, said of a section of the table, which the base book says of each part whose chapters are manuals; it is open when the reader is in its part, and closed it draws nothing of its own: The Entry and The Book. And the all-in-one book is the type of book whose every chapter is a manual, which the reference manual is and another manual extends in a line. A book's own theme supplies the colours and says in a few lines what steps aside while a manual chapter is open; nothing else knows the manual exists.
A part read as a manual is a context of its own, and that is what makes the appendix feel like its own reference manual inside another book. Reading the book, you do not see the manual's tree: the part's section stands as any section of the table, a heading and its rows, and you press a row to go in. In the context you see only the chapters of the part, as the manual's tree, with the book's own name at the head of the tree, and you press it to get out. The reference manual is all one manual, so its tree is always its tree and it has no way out.
An appendix read as a manual costs the chapter three lines and the table one. At the head of the chapter, before its title, the part and the view: a Part whose words are the part's name, and a Manual; then an Append for each file beside the chapter, as any chapter with files has. In the table, the section that lists the chapter is headed with the part's name, word for word, and said to be the appendix. Nothing else changes: no theme, no face, no class, and the book's other chapters say nothing. That is what The Catalogue, The Frame and my story's The Sheet each do.
A second reference manual is a book whose every chapter is read that way. Its book file is one line, a class extending the manual's all-in-one book, which brings the readings, the numbers, the light tone, the manual's theme and its numbered row, a folder of every section and the first chapter open when none is named. Its cover, synopsis and table are any book's, the table saying it is an index and wearing the manual's table face, its sections the groups. Every chapter says Manual at its head, opens with a paragraph said to be brief, which the book's own rule asks for, and appends its files. A chapter and a row in the catalogue shelve it. Five of those lines are the abstraction's and the rest are the book's own, as they are for any book here; the one I made to prove it is above.
What a maker has to know, each learned by breaking it. A part's heading in the table wears an id as every heading does, so a part is named so that no chapter's title wears the same one. The folder finds its section by the part's name, so the heading and the part say the same words, word for word, or the bind refuses it in a sentence. The brief stands directly under the title, before the sections. A format's rules enter the sheet before a theme's, so every rule of the tree says the book first and the folder open, and names the level's class beside the subclass's, the paragraph with the entry, the sentence with the heading, or it loses a tie to the theme; and a folder's layer stands between its section and the column that placed it, so what a theme said of the section's place at the foot it now says of the folder. When a page that should not have changed has, the proof is the library bound as it stood at the commit before, compared with the current one on every element and every property in every view, which is what found the three faults of the evening this was built.

<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&family=Source+Sans+3:wght@500;600;700&family=Source+Sans+3:wght@500;600;700&family=Source+Sans+3:wght@500;600;700&family=Source+Serif+4:ital,opsz,wght@0,8..60,400;0,8..60,600;0,8..60,700;1,8..60,400&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>
    /* ---- the page's palette, the bookshelf's: slate text, never black; a faint cool tint; the manual's own scheme on the body.
       The manual's two colours do quiet work: gunmetal, the band, is structure — the open row's strip, the lockup's ink;
       brass, the foot, is the code — a hairline under a heading, the numbers, the lit tab. The near-whites differ by side:
       the bar cool, the side bar grey, the reading column warm paper. ---- */
    :root {
        --paper: #fdfcfa; --text: #343c4a; --soft: #727d8c; --faint: #9ea8b5; --line: #e4e9f2; --tint: #f0f4fc; --bar-tint: #f8fafe;
        --side-tint: #f7f8fb; --read-tint: #fbfaf6;
        --sky: #e3edfb; --sky-ink: #4a6ea0; --wash: linear-gradient(135deg, #f1f5fd 0%, #fdfcfa 48%, #fdf5ee 100%);
        --sans: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; --serif: 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, serif; --between: 'Source Sans 3', 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; --mono: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
        --bar: 52px; --side: 272px; --space: 24px; --open: 184px; --radius: 6px;
        --beat: .22s;
    }
    /* each book's scheme, as its cover says it: the ground, the band and its ink, the foot and its ink, the drawing's ink */
    .library { --ground: #eef5f6; --band: #c3e3e6; --band-ink: #1c565c; --foot: #8db9bd; --foot-ink: #153e43; --ink: #1f5a60; }
    .story { --ground: #f5eedf; --band: #d9c3a3; --band-ink: #4a3626; --foot: #a3b6cc; --foot-ink: #2a4262; --ink: #2f4a6a; }
    .manual { --ground: #eef1f2; --band: #b6c1c6; --band-ink: #2b363c; --foot: #d8c48e; --foot-ink: #5d4a16; --ink: #4b3d14; }
    /* the night of the code, blended toward the manual's gunmetal; the brass dimmed into it for the numbers; and a light code */
    body.manual { --night: color-mix(in oklch, #0f2a33 55%, #2b363c); --dusk: color-mix(in oklch, #17363f 55%, #343f45); --dawn: color-mix(in oklch, #17363f 40%, #4a5560); --glow: #d6e1e3; --dim: color-mix(in oklch, #d8c48e 38%, #17363f); --brass: color-mix(in oklch, #d8c48e 72%, white); }
    body.manual[data-code="light"] { --night: #f6f7f4; --dusk: #eceee8; --dawn: #ffffff; --glow: #2b363c; --dim: color-mix(in oklch, #5d4a16 45%, white); --brass: #5d4a16; }
    * { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; }
    html, body { height: 100%; }
    body { display: grid; grid-template: var(--bar) auto / var(--side) minmax(0, 1fr); grid-template-areas: 'library library' 'holds leaves'; align-items: start; min-height: 100%; background: var(--wash); color: var(--text); font: 400 14px/1.6 var(--sans); }
    a { color: inherit; text-decoration: none; }
    [hidden] { display: none !important; }
    .pd-paragraph { margin: 0; }
    button { font: inherit; color: inherit; background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; cursor: pointer; }

    /* ---- the drawings and the marks, as the bookshelf draws them ---- */
    .pd-illustration { fill: none; stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 1.7; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }
    .pd-illustration .fill { fill: var(--foot); stroke: var(--ink); }
    .pd-illustration .light { fill: #ffffff; stroke: none; }
    .pd-mark { display: block; position: relative; flex: none; width: 28px; height: 28px; border: calc(var(--open) * 0.54 / 64 * 1.7) solid var(--ink); background: var(--band); overflow: hidden; }
    .pd-mark .pd-illustration { position: absolute; width: calc(var(--open) * 0.54); height: calc(var(--open) * 0.54); left: var(--window-x); top: var(--window-y); }

    /* ---- the bar is the cover. The two marks stand like two characters, four pixels apart, then the name; resting on the
       subject's mark turns the lockup into the subject's own — its mark alone, its name in its ink — and back. ---- */
    .pd-library { grid-area: library; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; display: flex; align-items: center; height: var(--bar); padding: 0 18px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fbfcfe 0%, #f8fafe 60%, #f1f4fa 100%); border-bottom: 1px solid #dfe4ed; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(43, 54, 60, .05); }
    .pd-lockup { display: flex; align-items: center; height: var(--bar); }
    .pd-lockup .pa-reference { display: block; }
    .pd-lockup .pd-mark { transition: width var(--beat) ease, margin var(--beat) ease, opacity var(--beat) ease, border-width var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-lockup .pd-mark.manual { margin-left: 4px; }
    .pd-lockup.subject .pd-mark.manual { width: 0; margin-left: 0; border-width: 0; opacity: 0; }
    .pd-names { display: grid; margin-left: 9px; }
    .pd-names .pd-name { grid-area: 1 / 1; font: 700 18px/1 var(--serif); letter-spacing: -0.015em; white-space: nowrap; transform: translateY(1px); transition: opacity var(--beat) ease, transform var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-names .pd-name.manual { color: #2b363c; font: 600 19px/1 var(--between); letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
    .pd-names .pd-name.library { color: #1c565c; opacity: 0; transform: translateY(7px); pointer-events: none; }
    .pd-lockup.subject .pd-name.library { pointer-events: auto; }
    .pd-lockup.subject .pd-name.manual { pointer-events: none; }
    .pd-lockup.subject .pd-name.manual { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-5px); }
    .pd-lockup.subject .pd-name.library { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(1px); }
    .pd-logo, .pd-subjects { display: none; }
    .pd-me { grid-area: library; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 4; justify-self: end; align-self: center; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; margin-right: 18px; }
    .pd-me .pd-byline { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; font-size: 13px; color: var(--soft); }
    .pd-me .pd-word.pa-reference { color: var(--text); font-weight: 500; }

    /* ---- the index is a file tree: groups as folders that fold, chapters as pages, their files beneath them ---- */
    .pd-holds { grid-area: holds; position: sticky; top: var(--bar); align-self: start; display: grid; grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr); height: calc(100vh - var(--bar)); padding: 14px 0 16px; overflow-y: auto; scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: transparent transparent; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #f9fafc 0%, #f7f8fb 86%, #f2f4f8 100%); border-right: 1px solid #e0e4eb; font-size: 12.5px; transition: scrollbar-color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-holds:hover { scrollbar-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--band) 62%, white) transparent; }
    .pd-holds::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 7px; }
    .pd-holds::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: transparent; border-radius: 4px; }
    .pd-holds:hover::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--band) 62%, white); }
    .pd-holds .pd-chapter { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 100%; }
    .pd-holds .pd-section { margin: 0 0 8px; }
    .pd-holds .pd-heading { display: none; }
    .pd-holds .pd-folder { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; width: 100%; height: 27px; padding: 0 14px 0 10px; text-align: left; font: 400 13px/27px var(--sans); color: #3a4452; transition: color var(--beat) ease, background var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-holds .pd-twist { flex: none; display: grid; place-items: center; width: 16px; height: 16px; color: #a5aebb; transition: transform .18s ease, color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-holds .pd-twist svg { width: 10px; height: 10px; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.6; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }
    .pd-holds .pd-twist.open { transform: rotate(90deg); }
    .pd-holds .pd-twist:hover { color: var(--text); }
    .pd-holds .pd-folder:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--sky) 30%, white); }
    .pd-holds .pd-section.folded .pd-container, .pd-holds .pd-section.folded .pd-file, .pd-holds .pd-section.folded .pd-key { display: none; }
    .pd-holds .pa-entry { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; margin: 0; height: 27px; padding: 0 14px 0 28px; font: 400 13px/27px var(--sans); color: #3a4452; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 transparent; transition: background var(--beat) ease, color var(--beat) ease, box-shadow var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-holds .pd-icon { flex: none; width: 14px; height: 14px; color: #a5aebb; transition: color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-holds .pa-entry .pa-content { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
    .pd-holds .pa-entry:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--sky) 40%, white); }
    .pd-holds .pa-entry.pa-open { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--sky) 72%, white); color: var(--band-ink); box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 var(--band-ink); }
    .pd-holds .pa-entry.pa-open .pd-icon { color: var(--band-ink); }
    .pd-holds .pa-number { font-size: 10.5px; color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--foot-ink) 48%, white); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
    .pd-holds .pd-file { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; width: 100%; height: 27px; padding: 0 14px 0 69px; text-align: left; font: 400 13px/27px var(--sans); color: #3a4452; transition: background var(--beat) ease, color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-holds .pd-file:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--sky) 40%, white); color: var(--text); }
    .pd-holds .pd-file.pa-open { color: var(--sky-ink); font-weight: 500; background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--sky) 45%, white); }
    .pd-holds .pa-parenthetical { display: none; }

    /* ---- a glyph per piece of code: one of seven kinds, a shape and a colour each, so related code looks related ---- */
    .kind-type { --kind-fill: #c3ccd2; --kind-ink: #26323a; }
    .kind-theme { --kind-fill: #e6d7a3; --kind-ink: #5a4610; }
    .kind-annotation { --kind-fill: #b3dde1; --kind-ink: #185056; }
    .kind-noun { --kind-fill: #bccde3; --kind-ink: #263e60; }
    .kind-layout { --kind-fill: #d4bfdb; --kind-ink: #553561; }
    .kind-face { --kind-fill: #e3c0b7; --kind-ink: #772f25; }
    .kind-tool { --kind-fill: #c6d6c1; --kind-ink: #3a5535; }
    .kind-folder { --kind-fill: #f1f3f5; --kind-ink: #8a94a3; }
    .pd-kind { flex: none; width: 16px; height: 16px; fill: none; stroke: var(--kind-ink); stroke-width: 1.25; stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-linecap: round; }
    .pd-kind .k-ground { fill: var(--kind-fill); stroke: var(--kind-ink); stroke-width: 1.5; }
    .pd-kind .k-dot { fill: var(--kind-ink); stroke: none; }
    .pd-kind .k-thin { stroke-width: .9; opacity: .7; }
    .pd-kind .k-over { fill: var(--kind-fill); }
    .pd-kind .k-solid { fill: var(--kind-ink); stroke: var(--kind-ink); }
    .pd-file-icon { flex: none; width: 13px; height: 13px; color: #9aa4b3; transition: color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-holds .pd-file.pa-open .pd-file-icon, .pd-tabs .pd-tab.pa-open .pd-file-icon, .pd-rail .pd-tab.pa-open .pd-file-icon, .pd-kinds .pd-kind-press.pa-open .pd-file-icon { color: var(--kind-ink); }
    .pd-holds .pd-key .pd-kind { width: 13px; height: 13px; }
    .pd-words .pd-title { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }
    .pd-words .pd-title .pd-kind { width: 22px; height: 22px; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-words .pd-title .pd-kind { width: 18px; height: 18px; }
    .pd-kinds { display: flex; gap: 6px; margin: 0 0 8px; }
    .pd-kinds .pd-kind-press { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; padding: 3px 8px 3px 5px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 999px; background: #ffffff; font: 500 11px/1 var(--mono); color: #6b7684; transition: border-color var(--beat) ease, color var(--beat) ease, background var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-kinds .pd-kind-press:hover { border-color: var(--kind-ink); color: var(--text); }
    .pd-kinds .pd-kind-press.pa-open { border-color: var(--kind-ink); background: var(--kind-fill); color: var(--kind-ink); }
    .pd-holds .pd-key { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 27px; padding: 0 14px 0 51px; font: 400 13px/27px var(--sans); color: #3a4452; }
    .pd-holds .pd-section.pd-key-section { margin-top: auto; padding-top: 8px; border-top: 1px solid #e3e7ee; }

    /* ---- the page in three states. Closed: the words run wide and the files are a rail at the right edge — a sliver of
       the black, which is the hint of what a press opens. Open: a file beside the words, in its black, on the right; its
       head is an editor's tab bar, the hint of the editor. Docked: the code is a tab in that bar, left against the side bar
       as in an editor, and the words step to a reading column on the right. ---- */
    .pd-leaves { grid-area: leaves; min-width: 0; }
    .pd-desk, .pd-switches, .pd-brief-bar { display: none; }
    .pd-leaf { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 0 48px; grid-template-areas: 'words panel rail'; min-height: calc(100vh - var(--bar)); transition: grid-template-columns .28s ease; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="open"] { grid-template-columns: minmax(380px, 1fr) min(44vw, 720px) 48px; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] { grid-template-areas: 'panel panel grip'; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 0 18px; height: calc(100vh - var(--bar)); }
    .pd-words { grid-area: words; min-width: 0; padding: 22px 36px 40px; overflow: hidden; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="open"] .pd-words { padding: 22px 28px 40px 32px; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-words { display: none; }
    .pd-grip { grid-area: grip; display: none; position: relative; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #f3f1eb 0%, #fbfaf6 10px); border-left: 1px solid #e6e2d8; cursor: pointer; transition: background var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-grip { display: block; }
    .pd-grip:hover { background: linear-gradient(90deg, #ece9e1 0%, #ffffff 10px); }
    .pd-grip .pd-skeleton { position: absolute; top: 14px; left: 5px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; width: 8px; opacity: .7; }
    .pd-grip .pd-skeleton i { display: block; height: 2px; border-radius: 1px; background: #cfcbc0; }
    .pd-words .pd-chapter { max-width: 104ch; }
    .pd-words .pd-title { font: 600 24px/1.2 var(--sans); letter-spacing: -0.02em; margin-bottom: 6px; color: #1a1f36; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-words .pd-title { font-size: 19px; }
    .pd-words .pa-brief { font: italic 400 15.5px/1.5 var(--serif); color: var(--soft); margin-bottom: 10px; max-width: 72ch; }
    .pd-words .pd-section { margin-top: 26px; }
    .pd-words .pd-heading { font: 600 11px/1.3 var(--sans); letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6b7684; padding-bottom: 6px; margin-bottom: 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); border-image: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--brass) 0 40px, var(--line) 40px) 1; }
    .pd-words .pd-paragraph { margin: 8px 0; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-words .pd-paragraph, .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-words .pa-brief { font-size: 13.5px; }
    .pd-words .pd-paragraph .pa-reference { color: var(--band-ink); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--band-ink) 35%, white); text-underline-offset: 2px; transition: text-decoration-color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-words .pd-paragraph .pa-reference:hover { text-decoration-color: var(--band-ink); }
    .pd-words .pa-self-reference { color: inherit; text-decoration: none; }
    .pd-words .pd-turn { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 24px; margin-top: 26px; font-size: 11px; }
    .pd-words .pd-turn .pd-count { color: var(--faint); }

    /* the rail: a sliver of the black, the files' names on it; gone when the editor's tab bar has them */
    .pd-rail { grid-area: rail; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; gap: 2px; padding: 10px 0; background: linear-gradient(90deg, color-mix(in oklch, var(--night) 82%, white) 0%, var(--night) 22%); box-shadow: inset 1px 0 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, .08); transition: background var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-rail { display: none; }
    .pd-rail .pd-tab { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 10px 0 8px; font: 500 11px/1 var(--mono); letter-spacing: .04em; color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--glow) 66%, var(--night)); border-left: 2px solid transparent; transition: background var(--beat) ease, color var(--beat) ease, border-color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-rail .pd-tab .pd-tab-name { writing-mode: vertical-rl; }
    .pd-rail .pd-skeleton { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 3px; width: 26px; margin-top: 2px; opacity: .55; transition: opacity var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-rail .pd-skeleton i { display: block; height: 2px; border-radius: 1px; background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--brass) 60%, var(--glow)); }
    .pd-rail .pd-tab:hover .pd-skeleton, .pd-rail .pd-tab.pa-open .pd-skeleton { opacity: .9; }
    .pd-rail .pd-tab:hover { color: var(--glow); background: var(--dusk); }
    .pd-rail .pd-tab.pa-open { color: var(--glow); border-left-color: var(--foot); background: var(--dusk); }

    /* the panel: the editor's tab bar at its head, the active file below; the options at the bar's end */
    .pd-files { grid-area: panel; display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr); min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; background: linear-gradient(90deg, color-mix(in oklch, var(--night) 90%, white) 0%, var(--night) 36px); color: var(--glow); box-shadow: -10px 0 18px -16px rgba(43, 54, 60, .5); transition: background var(--beat) ease, color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-files { box-shadow: none; }
    .pd-tabs .pd-words-only { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 0 12px; font: 500 10.5px/1 var(--sans); letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--glow) 62%, var(--night)); transition: color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-tabs .pd-words-only:hover { color: var(--glow); }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-tabs .pd-words-only { display: none; }
    .pd-tabs { display: flex; align-items: stretch; gap: 1px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, color-mix(in oklch, var(--dusk) 88%, white) 0%, var(--dusk) 100%); padding: 0 0 0 2px; border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--foot) 28%, var(--dusk)); }
    .pd-tabs .pd-tab { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; padding: 9px 14px 8px 12px; font: 500 12px/1 var(--mono); color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--glow) 62%, var(--night)); border-top: 2px solid transparent; transition: background var(--beat) ease, color var(--beat) ease, border-color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-tabs .pd-tab:hover { color: var(--glow); }
    .pd-tabs .pd-tab.pa-open { color: var(--glow); background: var(--night); border-top-color: var(--foot); }
    .pd-tabs .pd-dock { margin-left: auto; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 0 12px; font: 500 10.5px/1 var(--sans); letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--brass); transition: color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-tabs .pd-dock:hover { color: var(--glow); }
    .pd-tabs .pd-dock::before { content: ''; width: 9px; height: 9px; border: 1.5px solid currentColor; border-radius: 1px; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 -1.5px currentColor; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-tabs .pd-dock::before { box-shadow: -3px 3px 0 -1.5px currentColor; }
    .pd-options { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px; padding: 0 8px 0 4px; border-left: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--glow) 12%, transparent); }
    .pd-options .pd-option { padding: 5px 7px; font: 500 10.5px/1 var(--sans); letter-spacing: .04em; color: color-mix(in oklch, var(--glow) 55%, var(--night)); border-radius: 4px; transition: color var(--beat) ease, background var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-options .pd-option:hover { color: var(--glow); }
    .pd-options .pd-option[aria-pressed="true"] { color: var(--glow); background: var(--dawn); }
    .pd-listing { display: none; margin: 0; min-height: 0; }
    .pd-listing.pa-open { display: block; overflow: auto; scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: transparent transparent; transition: scrollbar-color var(--beat) ease; }
    .pd-listing.pa-open:hover { scrollbar-color: var(--dim) transparent; }
    .pd-listing .pd-word { display: none; }
    .pd-listing .pd-code { margin: 0; padding: 14px 0; font: 400 12px/1.7 var(--mono); white-space: normal; cursor: zoom-in; background: transparent; }
    .pd-leaf[data-panel="full"] .pd-listing .pd-code { cursor: default; }
    .pd-listing .pd-code code { background: transparent; color: inherit; }
    .pd-code-line { display: block; padding-right: 18px; white-space: pre; }
    .pd-leaf[data-wrap="on"] .pd-code-line { white-space: pre-wrap; padding-left: 58px; text-indent: -58px; }
    .pd-code-line::before { content: attr(data-line); display: inline-block; width: 44px; padding-right: 14px; text-align: right; color: var(--dim); user-select: none; text-indent: 0; }
    .pd-leaf[data-numbers="off"] .pd-code-line::before { content: ''; width: 14px; padding: 0; }

</style>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/highlight.js/11.9.0/styles/github-dark-dimmed.min.css" media="all" id="hljs-sheet">
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/highlight.js/11.9.0/highlight.min.js"></script>
</head>

<div class="pd-leaves">
<section class="pd-desk"></section>

<div class="pd-leaf" data-chapter="the-book" hidden><div class="pd-words"><div class="pd-chapter pd-canonical pa-open pa-page"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-book" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-book" class="pd-sentence pd-title pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-referent">The Book</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph pa-brief">The class every book of this library stands on: it draws the frame once and collects its chapters.</div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#what-the-book-is" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="what-the-book-is" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">What the book is</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">Every book in this library extends one class, so what a book is here is said once. A book of mine holds chapters and nothing else, it has a place for every chapter it holds, and only an ordinary chapter appends a file. The class says all three in its specification, and the bind holds every book to it.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">The class draws the frame that is on every screen, in five regions named as the frame&#x27;s sketch names them: the library&#x27;s bar, with what the book is filed under and the library&#x27;s own subjects; me, who the book is by; what the book holds, its table of contents; the head, its cover and its switches; and the leaves, the front it opens on and then one leaf for each chapter, the chapter with the files it appends. A region is a method, and a type of book overrides the method whose region it fills differently, and nothing else.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#how-the-book-fits-the-librarys-patterns" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="how-the-book-fits-the-librarys-patterns" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">How the book fits the library&#x27;s patterns</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The purpose of a book is layout: the book&#x27;s own class places its parts, each in an element of its own with a class, and it finds its chapters by what they carry, never by position. Where the regions go is not the book&#x27;s to say; that is <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-layout" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the layout</span></a>, said of the book once, whose one grid is the frame: the library&#x27;s bar across the top, what the book holds down the side. What colours the regions is <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-tone" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">a tone</span></a>, said of the book too. The class gives every book its layout and its tone when it is defined, and a type of book that wants another tone registers it on its class in one line, the way the framework&#x27;s own theme is registered.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#how-the-book-is-used" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="how-the-book-is-used" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">How the book is used</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">A type of book is a class under this one. <a href="/dougs-library/#the-catalogue" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">The catalogue</span></a> overrides what the book opens on, to put its shelf under its synopsis with its own cover first, its head, which it leaves to its switches, and its front, which is always open, and names its entries as pages; <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-manual" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the manual</span></a> overrides its switches and gives itself the spread that sets a chapter beside its file; <a href="/dougs-story/#the-sheet" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">my story</span></a> overrides its head and its front, and <a href="/dougs-design/#the-frame" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the design book</span></a> says which chapter opens when none is named. Each is a few lines, because the frame is this class&#x27;s.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#what-the-book-gives-a-type" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="what-the-book-gives-a-type" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">What the book gives a type</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">What a type reads: its chapters, the ordinary ones; what it places, which its specification counts; which chapter is open, the one the address names, whether the address names the chapter or a heading inside it; the three tones it may offer as switches. What a type overrides: the library&#x27;s bar, the subjects, what the book holds, the head, the front, what the book opens on, the leaves, the switches, the listings a chapter&#x27;s files are printed as.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#where-the-book-bites" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="where-the-book-bites" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">Where the book bites</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">A type overrides a region and never redraws the frame; a type that wrote its own bars was the wrong turn this class ended. A thing said of a book of this library takes the one rule in the second file below, so it is said of a book of this library and of nothing else. And the class imports the library&#x27;s subjects from the catalogue through a file beside that book&#x27;s chapter which imports only the framework, because the catalogue&#x27;s table imports this manual&#x27;s door, and a cycle through the door loads half a module.</div></div><div class="pd-paragraph pd-turn"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-book" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-before">← <!-- -->The Book</span></a><span class="pd-word pd-count">1 of 17</span><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-listing" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-after">The Listing<!-- --> →</span></a></div></div></div><div class="pd-files"><div class="pd-paragraph pd-listing"><span class="pd-word">code.tsx</span><pre class="pd-letter pd-figure pd-code"><code><span class="pd-code-line" data-line="1"><span>import</span> { <span>ReactNode</span> } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;react&#x27;</span>;</span>

<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="2"><span>import</span> { $Writing, <span>AnnotationSpecification</span>, specify } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;@dna-platform/public&#x27;</span>;</span>

<div class="pd-leaf" data-chapter="the-theme" hidden><div class="pd-words"><div class="pd-chapter pd-canonical pa-page"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-theme" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-theme" class="pd-sentence pd-title pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-referent">The Theme</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph pa-brief">Every value the library&#x27;s rules read, declared once, and the parts that dress the frame.</div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#what-the-theme-is" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="what-the-theme-is" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">What the theme is</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The theme is where this library keeps its values, and the one styled component every book is drawn inside. The framework&#x27;s own theme has no values and no rules, so everything here is mine. Its values are the frame&#x27;s sketch&#x27;s own, named as that file names them, by role: the bar and what is read on it — the bar, its ink, its dim ink, what is on, its line, the mark; the side bar and what is read on it; the paper and the ink, the soft and the line; the orange that is me, one serif and one sans; the width of the side bar; the faces, sizes and spaces. Five of them are the ones a book sets to have a colour scheme of its own — its colour, its accent, its side bar, its paper and its ink — and the frame reads those and nothing else, so every book not yet written has a scheme the moment it sets five values.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#how-the-theme-fits-the-librarys-patterns" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="how-the-theme-fits-the-librarys-patterns" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">How the theme fits the library&#x27;s patterns</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">Every value the library reads is declared here, so a rule anywhere reads it and a template anywhere is typed against one theme; a book&#x27;s own theme sets values and adds parts, and declares nothing. The rules are parts, each a method that returns some rules for one thing on the page — the page, the writing, the links, the figures, the listings, the switches, the turns, the library&#x27;s bar, the head, the holds, the tones — composed once in the field that holds the component, so a book&#x27;s theme changes one part and keeps the rest. What a reader switches is never a part: <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-tone" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">a tone</span></a>, a reading, a paper each add a class, and the parts that read those classes are here, always.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#how-the-theme-is-used" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="how-the-theme-is-used" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">How the theme is used</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">A book&#x27;s theme is a class under this one, registered on the book&#x27;s class in one line. <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-manual" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">The manual&#x27;s</span></a> sets its measure, its spread&#x27;s column and the teal of its sketch as its colour, accent and side bar, and adds the parts for its index and its words; the catalogue&#x27;s keeps the base&#x27;s values, which are the site&#x27;s own, and adds the parts for its front and its covers; my story&#x27;s sets its prose face, its amber on book paper and its three papers&#x27; values; the design book&#x27;s its rose on white.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#where-the-theme-bites" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="where-the-theme-bites" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">Where the theme bites</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">A part of a theme must not take the name of a value the theme declares, nor of a member the class has, nor of a part the base already has unless it says it overrides and spreads the base&#x27;s into its own: each of these happened once — a part named side, a part named frame, a part named cards, a part named head — and each broke the page somewhere else without a word. The typecheck in the binder&#x27;s folder names the first two kinds; the third it does not, so the base&#x27;s part names are listed in each book&#x27;s chapter. A value that would be computed from another is computed in the template, never in a field, or a book that changes the first never reaches the second.</div></div><div class="pd-paragraph pd-turn"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-listing" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-before">← <!-- -->The Listing</span></a><span class="pd-word pd-count">3 of 17</span><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-date" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-after">The Date<!-- --> →</span></a></div></div></div><div class="pd-files"><div class="pd-paragraph pd-listing"><span class="pd-word">code.tsx</span><pre class="pd-letter pd-figure pd-code"><code><span class="pd-code-line" data-line="1"><span>import</span> { <span>ElementType</span> } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;react&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="2"><span>import</span> { css, <span>RuleSet</span> } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;styled-components&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="3"><span>import</span> { $, selection } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;@dna-platform/chemistry&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="4"><span>import</span> { $Theme } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;@dna-platform/public&#x27;</span>;</span>

<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="6"><span>declare</span> <span>module</span> <span>&#x27;styled-components&#x27;</span> {</span>
