<div class="pd-leaf" data-chapter="developing-a-library" hidden><div class="pd-words"><div class="pd-chapter pd-canonical pa-page"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#developing-a-library" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="developing-a-library" class="pd-sentence pd-title pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-referent">Developing a Library</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph pa-brief">How a page of this library is worked on with the page open, and bound once.</div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#the-page-stays-open" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-page-stays-open" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">The page stays open</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">I develop this library with its pages open. The binder serves the library live, straight from the files I am writing, and when I save one the open page changes in place: a sentence in a chapter in a quarter of a second, a rule in a theme in about half of one. Nothing is bound and the page is not loaded again. If what I saved breaks the library, the page says so in the compiler&#x27;s own sentence, and the sentence goes when I mend the file.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">This is the only way I look at the library while I am working on it. Work on how a page looks needs its answer at once, and a way of working that cannot give one has failed at what it is for.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#the-workbench" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-workbench" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">The workbench</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The workbench is the tool I do this with. Opened once, it starts the live site and keeps a browser open on it. After that I ask it for a look at any book. It waits for my last save to reach the page, photographs the page at a desk&#x27;s width or a phone&#x27;s, and tells me:</div><div class="pd-container"><div class="pd-paragraph pa-list"><div class="pd-sentence pd-line pa-item">what the page says, or any part of it;</div><div class="pd-sentence pd-line pa-item">what a rule computes to on an element, and where the element is;</div><div class="pd-sentence pd-line pa-item">how many things run past the right edge of the screen;</div><div class="pd-sentence pd-line pa-item">anything that went wrong on the page, and what the compiler says is wrong if it stopped.</div></div></div><div class="pd-paragraph">A look takes under a second, because the browser is already open and the page is already drawn. It can press something first, load the page again as a reader arriving would, and say which of the rules that name a thing wins. What the workbench does for a book is what <a href="/dougs-design/#the-camera" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the camera</span></a> does for a concept, and it is kept here for the same reason the camera is kept there, which is told in <a href="/dougs-story/#closure" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">Closure</span></a>.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#when-i-bind" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="when-i-bind" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">When I bind</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The bind is how the library is published, and it is not how I look at it. What it does is said in <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#initializing-a-library" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">Initializing a Library</span></a>. It takes seconds where a save takes none, so I bind when a piece of work is done.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">The bind checks three things the live site does not: each book against its own rules, each page as it is printed for a reader who arrives before the code does, and every link against the page it leads to. So my last look at finished work is at the site the bind built, loaded afresh, and the workbench takes that look too.</div></div><div class="pd-paragraph pd-turn"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#initializing-a-library" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-before">← <!-- -->Initializing a Library</span></a><span class="pd-word pd-count">6 of 17</span><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-author-and-the-subject" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-after">The Author and the Subject<!-- --> →</span></a></div></div></div><div class="pd-files"><div class="pd-paragraph pd-listing"><span class="pd-word">workbench.mjs</span><pre class="pd-letter pd-figure pd-code"><code><span class="pd-code-line" data-line="1"><span>// The workbench: the library served live from its sources, a browser kept open on it, and a way to ask that</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="2"><span>// browser what a page looks like. Open it once and leave it open:</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="3"><span>//</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="4"><span>//     node .me/.manual/6-developing-a-library~workbench.mjs</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="5"><span>//</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="6"><span>// Then look at a book from another terminal, as often as needed:</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="7"><span>//</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="8"><span>//     node .me/.manual/6-developing-a-library~workbench.mjs look dougs-story</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="9"><span>//     node .me/.manual/6-developing-a-library~workbench.mjs look dougs-story/#closure phone at=.pd-title</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="10"><span>//</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="11"><span>// A look waits for the last save to reach the page, prints what it found and says where it put the photograph.</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="12"><span>// After the book&#x27;s address it takes, in any order:</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="13"><span>//</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="14"><span>//     phone                          a phone&#x27;s width, where a desk&#x27;s is the default</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="15"><span>//     built                          the site the last bind built, served on 4242, where the live one is the default</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="16"><span>//     fresh                          load the page again first, as a reader arriving would</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="17"><span>//     whole                          photograph the whole page, where the screen is the default</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="18"><span>//     at=&lt;selector&gt;                  photograph that element alone</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="19"><span>//     click=&lt;selector&gt;               press it first</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="20"><span>//     read=&lt;selector&gt;                print what each match says</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="21"><span>//     style=&lt;selector&gt;|&lt;property&gt;    print what each match computes to, the properties separated by commas</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="22"><span>//     box=&lt;selector&gt;                 print where each match is</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="23"><span>//     tree=&lt;selector&gt;|&lt;depth&gt;        print the elements under the first match, each with its classes and its size</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="24"><span>//     after=&lt;selector&gt;               print what is drawn before and after the first match</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="25"><span>//     rules=&lt;word&gt;|&lt;property&gt;        print every rule whose selector holds the word, in the order they apply</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="26"><span>//     out=&lt;file&gt;                     where the photograph goes</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="27"><span>//</span></span>

<div class="pd-leaf" data-chapter="the-cover" hidden><div class="pd-words"><div class="pd-chapter pd-canonical pa-page"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-cover" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-cover" class="pd-sentence pd-title pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-referent">The Cover</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph pa-brief">The cover is a book&#x27;s data model: what it says is said in annotations, this cover type exposes each as a property, and any part of the book imports the cover rather than the whole book to read it.</div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#what-the-cover-carries" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="what-the-cover-carries" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">What the cover carries</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The framework&#x27;s cover says the book&#x27;s title, its author and the subject it is filed under, and that is what the bar across the top of every page shows. A design that needs more of a book says more on its cover, as annotations, so that the cover stays the one place a book describes itself. For the bookshelf a cover carries three more things: its scheme — the six colours of its jacket, the ground, the band and its ink, the foot and its ink, and the ink its drawing is drawn in; its illustration, a drawing kept as a file beside the cover and drawn by the cover itself; and its window, where the mark that stands for the book in a bar is cut from that drawing. The cover type here exposes them as properties, and its specification refuses a cover that lacks one.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#how-another-books-cover-reaches-a-catalogue" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="how-another-books-cover-reaches-a-catalogue" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">How another book&#x27;s cover reaches a catalogue</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">A catalogue&#x27;s chapter that stands for a book already imports that book&#x27;s own synopsis, and the framework&#x27;s synopsis appends its words. The same chapter holds that book&#x27;s cover the same way, said as a volume: the cover is imported and held as data, and nothing of it is appended, so nothing of it draws. The shelf and the desk read the volume&#x27;s cover and draw a jacket from it; the bar reads a cover and draws a mark from it. That is how a page knows another book: by importing its cover, never by looking it up, and never by drawing it twice.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">The jacket and the mark are the two things drawn from a cover. A jacket is the cover as a reader sees it on the shelf and on the desk: the name on the band, the drawing on the ground, the author on the foot, in the scheme&#x27;s six colours. A mark is a window onto the same drawing at the desk&#x27;s scale, a square with the drawing&#x27;s own line as its border, so that the same drawing is the same everywhere and a change to the file changes every place it stands. <a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-bookshelf" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">The Bookshelf</span></a> dresses both.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">The browser&#x27;s tab wears the same mark. The tool beside this chapter makes the library&#x27;s icon from the catalogue&#x27;s cover — the drawing&#x27;s file, the scheme, the window — as the mark the bar draws, and writes it into the binding&#x27;s configuration, so the tab changes when the cover does. It is run when the cover changes, before a bind.</div></div><div class="pd-paragraph pd-turn"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-colour" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-before">← <!-- -->The Colour</span></a><span class="pd-word pd-count">16 of 17</span><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-bookshelf" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-after">The Bookshelf<!-- --> →</span></a></div></div></div><div class="pd-files"><div class="pd-paragraph pd-listing"><span class="pd-word">code.tsx</span><pre class="pd-letter pd-figure pd-code"><code><span class="pd-code-line" data-line="1"><span>import</span> { <span>ElementType</span>, <span>ReactNode</span> } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;react&#x27;</span>;</span>

<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="249"></span></code></pre></div><div class="pd-paragraph pd-listing"><span class="pd-word">icon.mjs</span><pre class="pd-letter pd-figure pd-code"><code><span class="pd-code-line" data-line="1"><span>// The library&#x27;s icon, made from its catalogue&#x27;s cover: the mark as the bar draws it — the drawing</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="2"><span>// windowed at the desk&#x27;s scale, grounded in the band, bordered with the drawing&#x27;s own line — written</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="3"><span>// into the binding&#x27;s configuration as the page&#x27;s icon. Run it when the cover changes:</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="4"><span>//   node .me/.manual/19-the-cover~icon.mjs</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="5"><span>import</span> { readFileSync, writeFileSync } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;node:fs&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="6"><span>import</span> { resolve } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;node:path&#x27;</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="7"></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="8"><span>const</span> me = <span>resolve</span>(<span>import</span>.<span>meta</span>.<span>dirname</span>, <span>&#x27;..&#x27;</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="9"><span>const</span> cover = <span>readFileSync</span>(<span>resolve</span>(me, <span>&#x27;..reference/.cover.tsx&#x27;</span>), <span>&#x27;utf8&#x27;</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="10"><span>const</span> drawing = <span>readFileSync</span>(<span>resolve</span>(me, <span>&#x27;..reference/.cover~illustration.svg&#x27;</span>), <span>&#x27;utf8&#x27;</span>).<span>trim</span>();</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="11"><span>const</span> configuration = <span>resolve</span>(me, <span>&#x27;..public/.binding/.pubconfig&#x27;</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="12"></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="13"><span>const</span> <span>said</span> = (<span>name</span>) =&gt; cover.<span>match</span>(<span>new</span> <span>RegExp</span>(<span>`<span>${name}</span>=&quot;([^&quot;]+)&quot;`</span>, <span>&#x27;u&#x27;</span>))?.[<span>1</span>];</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="14"><span>const</span> band = <span>said</span>(<span>&#x27;band&#x27;</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="15"><span>const</span> foot = <span>said</span>(<span>&#x27;foot&#x27;</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="16"><span>const</span> ink = <span>said</span>(<span>&#x27;ink&#x27;</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="17"><span>const</span> x = <span>Number</span>(<span>said</span>(<span>&#x27;x&#x27;</span>));</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="18"><span>const</span> y = <span>Number</span>(<span>said</span>(<span>&#x27;y&#x27;</span>));</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="19"></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="20"><span>const</span> mark = <span>28</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="21"><span>const</span> volume = <span>184</span>;</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="22"><span>const</span> <span>round</span> = (<span>number</span>) =&gt; <span>Number</span>(number.<span>toFixed</span>(<span>3</span>));</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="23"><span>const</span> scale = <span>round</span>(volume * <span>0.54</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="24"><span>const</span> line = <span>round</span>(scale / <span>64</span> * <span>1.7</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="25"><span>const</span> inner = drawing.<span>replace</span>(<span>&#x27;&lt;svg &#x27;</span>, <span>`&lt;svg x=&quot;<span>${round(line + x)}</span>&quot; y=&quot;<span>${round(line + y)}</span>&quot; width=&quot;<span>${scale}</span>&quot; height=&quot;<span>${scale}</span>&quot; `</span>);</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="26"><span>const</span> svg = [</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="27">    <span>`&lt;svg xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot; viewBox=&quot;0 0 <span>${mark}</span> <span>${mark}</span>&quot;&gt;`</span>,</span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="28">    <span>`&lt;style&gt;.pd-illustration{fill:none;stroke:<span>${ink}</span>;stroke-width:1.7;stroke-linecap:round;stroke-linejoin:round}.pd-illustration .fill{fill:<span>${foot}</span>;stroke:<span>${ink}</span>}.pd-illustration .light{fill:#ffffff;stroke:none}&lt;/style&gt;`</span>,</span>

<div class="pd-leaf" data-chapter="the-bookshelf" hidden><div class="pd-words"><div class="pd-chapter pd-canonical pa-page"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-bookshelf" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-bookshelf" class="pd-sentence pd-title pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-referent">The Bookshelf</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph pa-brief">A catalogue whose page is a shelf, and its theme: the bar is the cover, the side bar is the table of contents, the open book lies on a desk above the shelf, and every book is a jacket in its own six colours.</div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#the-catalogue-a-type-of-book" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-catalogue-a-type-of-book" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">The catalogue, a type of book</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">A catalogue is a book whose chapters stand for other books: a chapter that carries another book&#x27;s synopsis, and holds that book&#x27;s cover as a volume, is one of its books. The class finds them by what they carry and draws the regions the base gives every book in its own way — the bar as its cover, with the subject&#x27;s mark first when the book is filed under another and no mark when it is filed under itself, as only the library is; the side bar as its table; the open leaf as the desk, the jacket large beside the chapter&#x27;s words, and the shelf of jackets after the leaves. Three things are said in it: a caption, of the one line an entry says; an arrow, of the word in a row that leads to the book; and unfolded, of the book, by the switch that reads on. A title in a catalogue&#x27;s entry refers to the book it stands for, by a reference registered on the class. A library makes its catalogue by saying so in its door, in one line, and writing its entries.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#what-the-theme-dresses" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="what-the-theme-dresses" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">What the theme dresses</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The bookshelf was designed as one page in HTML, in <a href="/dougs-design/#the-bookshelf" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference">the design book</span></a>, and this theme is that page&#x27;s style carried into the library&#x27;s words. The page&#x27;s values are its fields: a slate ink and never black, a faint cool tint, one sky accent for the library itself, a bar of fifty-two pixels, a side bar of two hundred and thirty-two, a cover of a hundred and thirty-two on the shelf and a hundred and eighty-four on the desk, all of it on a body of fourteen. Its parts dress what the catalogue draws: the illustrations and the marks, the lockups in the bar, the shelf, the jackets, the desk, the page unfolded to read on, and the page in its built view.</div><div class="pd-paragraph">A jacket is the same for every book: three bands of three colours, the name on the band above, the drawing on the ground between, the author on the foot, hairlines of white parting them as Penguin&#x27;s did. The colours are the cover&#x27;s own scheme, read from the cover and set where the jacket is drawn, so the theme knows no book by name and a new book brings its colours with it. A mark is a window onto the same drawing, at the desk&#x27;s scale, bordered with the drawing&#x27;s own line. In the bar the marks and the name stand one gap apart, the same gap three times, and resting on the subject&#x27;s mark unfolds the subject&#x27;s name in the book&#x27;s own formatting, in the book&#x27;s place.</div></div><div class="pd-section"><a href="#the-two-views" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><div id="the-two-views" class="pd-sentence pd-heading pa-referent pa-reference pa-self-reference">The two views</div></a><div class="pd-paragraph">The page has two views and one table of contents. Reading, the contents stand first and the page is the desk and the shelf; built, the appendix stands first, the shelf and the desk step aside, and the open chapter is shown with its files as the reference manual shows a chapter. Which view stands is a class on the book that the layout adds when the open chapter is in the appendix, so the toggle between them is a press on a row of the other group. The built view borrows the manual&#x27;s look for now; it is designed properly when the manual is.</div></div><div class="pd-paragraph pd-turn"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-cover" class="pa-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-before">← <!-- -->The Cover</span></a><span class="pd-word pd-count">17 of 17</span><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/#the-bookshelf" class="pa-reference pa-self-reference pd-container"><span class="pd-word pa-reference pa-self-reference pa-after">The Bookshelf<!-- --> →</span></a></div></div></div><div class="pd-files"><div class="pd-paragraph pd-listing"><span class="pd-word">code.tsx</span><pre class="pd-letter pd-figure pd-code"><code><span class="pd-code-line" data-line="1"><span>import</span> { <span>ReactNode</span> } <span>from</span> <span>&#x27;react&#x27;</span>;</span>

<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="530"><span>            <span>.pa-built</span> <span>.pd-listing</span> <span>.pd-word</span> {</span></span>

<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="534"><span>                <span>padding</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> * <span>0.292</span>) <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> / <span>2</span>);</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="535"><span>                <span>border-block-end</span>: thin solid </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.sideLine}</span><span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="536"><span>                <span>border-radius</span>: <span>0</span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="537"><span>                <span>background</span>: </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.white}</span><span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="538"><span>                <span>font-size</span>: <span>calc</span>(<span>0.857</span> * </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.size}</span><span>);</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="539"><span>                <span>font-weight</span>: <span>500</span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="540"><span>                <span>line-height</span>: <span>1</span>;</span></span>

<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="542"><span>            }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="543"><span>            <span>.pa-built</span> <span>.pd-listing</span> <span>.pd-word</span><span>::before</span> { <span>content</span>: <span>&#x27;&#x27;</span>; <span>width</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> * <span>0.292</span>); <span>height</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> * <span>0.292</span>); <span>border-radius</span>: <span>50%</span>; <span>background</span>: </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.skyInk}</span><span>; <span>opacity</span>: <span>0.6</span>; }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="544"><span>            <span>.pa-built</span> <span>.pd-listing</span> <span>.pd-code</span> {</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="545"><span>                <span>margin</span>: <span>0</span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="546"><span>                <span>padding</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> / <span>2</span>) <span>0</span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="547"><span>                <span>border-radius</span>: <span>0</span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="548"><span>                <span>background</span>: none;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="549"><span>                <span>font-size</span>: <span>calc</span>(<span>0.893</span> * </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.size}</span><span>);</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="550"><span>                <span>line-height</span>: <span>1.65</span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="551"><span>                <span>color</span>: </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.sideInk}</span><span>;</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="552"><span>            }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="553"><span>            <span>.pa-built</span> <span>.pd-code-line</span><span>::before</span> { <span>width</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> * <span>1.833</span>); <span>padding-inline-end</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> * <span>0.583</span>); <span>color</span>: </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.faint}</span><span>; }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="554"><span>        `</span>;</span>

<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="560"><span>                <span>.pd-leaves</span> { <span>padding</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> * <span>0.667</span>); }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="561"><span>                <span>.pd-logo</span> { <span>margin-inline-end</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> / <span>2</span>); }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="562"><span>                <span>.pd-me</span> <span>.pd-word</span><span>.pd-mark</span> { <span>display</span>: block; }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="563"><span>                <span>.pd-leaf</span><span>.pd-open</span> { <span>grid-template-columns</span>: </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.cover}</span><span> <span>minmax</span>(<span>0</span>, <span>1</span>fr); <span>gap</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> * <span>0.667</span>); <span>padding</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.space}</span><span> * <span>0.667</span>); }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="564"><span>                <span>.pd-leaf</span><span>.pd-open</span> <span>.pd-paragraph</span><span>.pd-jacket</span> { <span>width</span>: </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.cover}</span><span>; <span>height</span>: <span>calc</span>(</span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.cover}</span><span> * <span>1.5</span>); <span>font-size</span>: <span>calc</span>(<span>0.964</span> * </span><span>${({ theme }) =&gt; theme.size}</span><span>); }</span></span>
<span class="pd-code-line" data-line="565"><span>                <span>.pd-leaf</span><span>.pd-open</span> <span>.pd-words</span> { <span>max-height</span>: none; }</span></span>

</div>
<script>
    // The three covers' drawings, as their files beside the covers hold them, and where each cover cuts its mark.
    const drawings = {
        library: '<svg viewBox="0 0 64 64" class="pd-illustration"><path class="light" d="M9 7h46v50H9z"/><path d="M9 7h46v50H9zM9 24h46M9 41h46"/><path class="fill" d="M13 11h5v13h-5zM20 9h4v15h-4zM26 13h6v11h-6zM34 10h4v14h-4zM40 14h6v10h-6z"/><path d="M48 24l4-12 3 1-4 11z"/><path class="fill" d="M13 28h4v13h-4zM19 30h7v11h-7zM28 27h4v14h-4zM34 31h5v10h-5zM41 28h6v13h-6zM49 29h3v12h-3z"/><path class="fill" d="M13 46h6v11h-6zM21 44h4v13h-4zM27 47h8v10h-8zM37 45h4v12h-4zM43 48h6v9h-6z"/><path d="M50 57l3-11 3 1-3 10z"/></svg>',
        manual: '<svg viewBox="0 0 64 64" class="pd-illustration"><circle class="fill" cx="24" cy="41" r="10"/><circle class="light" cx="24" cy="41" r="3.5"/><circle cx="24" cy="41" r="3.5"/><path d="M24 28v-4M24 54v4M11 41H7M37 41h4M15 32l-3-3M33 32l3-3M15 50l-3 3M33 50l3 3"/><path class="fill" d="M38 10l5-5 9 9-5 5-4-1L31 30l-5-5 12-12z"/><path d="M38 10l5-5 9 9-5 5-4-1L31 30l-5-5 12-12zM44 12l3 3"/></svg>',
        story: '<svg viewBox="0 0 64 64" class="pd-illustration"><path class="light" d="M8 13h23v38H8zM33 13h23v38H33z"/><path d="M8 13h23v38H8zM33 13h23v38H33z"/><path d="M13 21h13M13 27h13M13 33h9M38 21h13M38 27h13M38 33h13M38 39h8"/><path class="fill" d="M15 55 45 25l4 4-30 30-6 2z"/><path d="M15 55 45 25l4 4-30 30-6 2zM43 27l4 4M17 53l2 2"/></svg>',
    };
    const windows = { library: [-46, -13], manual: [-23, -50], story: [-54, -33] };
    const mark = (key) => '<span class="pd-mark ' + key + '" style="--window-x: ' + windows[key][0] + 'px; --window-y: ' + windows[key][1] + 'px">' + drawings[key] + '</span>';
    const icons = {
        page: '<svg class="pd-icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 2h5l3 3v9H4z"/><path d="M9 2v3h3"/><path d="M6 8h4M6 10.5h4" stroke-linecap="round"/></svg>',
    };
    // a glyph per piece of code: its kind is its name's word, and the chapter's own code is the chapter's kind
    // every mark is a square of one family with the site's: the kind's ink as its border, the kind's pastel as its ground, an
    // abstract figure in the ink — a spine and two shelves for a type of book, three dots for a theme, a tag's corner for a thing
    // said, a nib for a thing drawn, a grid for a layout, a square over a square for a face, a hub with its ticks for a tool
    // closed shapes, or shapes that meet the border — never a floating line
    const glyphs = {
        type: '<path d="M5.5 .75v14.5M5.5 6h9.75M5.5 10h9.75"/>',
        theme: '<circle cx="5.5" cy="6" r="1.6" class="k-dot"/><circle cx="10.5" cy="5.5" r="1.6" class="k-dot"/><circle cx="8" cy="10.5" r="1.6" class="k-dot"/>',
        annotation: '<path d="M.75 8 8 .75 15.25 8 8 15.25z"/><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="1.4" class="k-dot"/>',
        noun: '<path d="M.75 15.25 10 6l2 2-9.25 9.25z" class="k-solid"/><path d="M10 6l2.5-2.5 2.5 2.5L12.5 8.5"/>',
        layout: '<path d="M.75 6.5h14.5M8 6.5v8.75"/>',
        face: '<path d="M.75 .75h9v9h-9z"/><path d="M6.25 6.25h9v9h-9z" class="k-over"/>',
        tool: '<circle cx="8" cy="8" r="2.6" class="k-dot"/><path d="M8 .75v3.5M8 11.75v3.5M.75 8h3.5M11.75 8h3.5"/>',
    };
    const fileIcon = '<svg class="pd-icon pd-file-icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M6 4.5 3.5 8 6 11.5M10 4.5 12.5 8 10 11.5"/></svg>';
    const names = { type: 'a type of book', theme: 'a theme', annotation: 'a thing said of a writing', noun: 'a thing the library draws', layout: 'a layout', face: 'a face', tool: 'a tool' };
    const chapters = { 'the-book': 'type', 'the-theme': 'theme', 'the-cover': 'annotation', 'the-bookshelf': 'type', 'developing-a-library': 'tool', 'the-manual': 'type', 'the-layout': 'layout', 'the-turn': 'noun', 'the-switch': 'noun', 'the-listing': 'noun', 'the-author-and-the-subject': 'noun', 'the-entry': 'annotation', 'the-tone': 'annotation', 'the-first': 'annotation', 'the-colour': 'annotation', 'the-date': 'annotation', 'initializing-a-library': 'tool' };
    const kindOf = (chapter, file) => {
        const word = file.replace(/\..*$/u, '');
        if (word === 'code') return chapters[chapter] ?? 'noun';
        if (word in glyphs) return word;
        return { said: 'annotation', entry: 'annotation', forward: 'annotation', faces: 'face', views: 'annotation', icon: 'tool', workbench: 'tool', subjects: 'annotation', booklink: 'annotation' }[word] ?? chapters[chapter] ?? 'noun';
    };
    const glyph = (kind) => '<svg class="pd-kind kind-' + kind + '" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect x="0.75" y="0.75" width="14.5" height="14.5" class="k-ground"/>' + glyphs[kind] + '</svg>';
    const folder = '<svg class="pd-kind kind-folder" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><rect x="0.75" y="0.75" width="14.5" height="14.5" class="k-ground"/><path d="M3.5 5.5h3l1.5 1.5h4.5v5h-9z"/></svg>';
    const languages = { tsx: 'typescript', ts: 'typescript', mjs: 'javascript', js: 'javascript', css: 'css', html: 'xml', svg: 'xml', json: 'json', md: 'markdown' };
    document.body.classList.add('manual');
    document.body.dataset.code = 'dark';

    // the bar is the cover: the two marks as two characters, the subject's first, then the book's name — and the subject's name
    // in its own ink waiting underneath, for the rest on the subject's mark
    const logo = document.querySelector('.pd-logo');
    logo.insertAdjacentHTML('beforebegin',
        '<div class="pd-lockup">'
        + '<a href="/dougs-library/" class="pa-reference pd-container">' + mark('library') + '</a>'
        + '<a href="/dougs-reference-manual/" class="pa-reference pd-container">' + mark('manual') + '</a>'
        + '<span class="pd-names"><a href="/dougs-reference-manual/" class="pd-name manual">Dougs Reference Manual</a><a href="/dougs-library/" class="pd-name library">Dougs Library</a></span>'
        + '</div>');
    document.querySelector('.pd-me').insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', '<span class="story">' + mark('story') + '</span>');
    const lockup = document.querySelector('.pd-lockup');
    lockup.querySelector('.pd-mark.library').addEventListener('mouseenter', () => lockup.classList.add('subject'));
    lockup.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => lockup.classList.remove('subject'));

    // the code, highlighted by the file's language, every language the highlighter knows
    const highlight = (listing, file) => {
        if (!window.hljs) return;
        const language = languages[file.split('.').pop()] ?? 'plaintext';
        for (const line of listing.querySelectorAll('.pd-code-line'))
            line.innerHTML = window.hljs.highlight(line.textContent, { language, ignoreIllegals: true }).value;
        listing.querySelector('code')?.classList.add('hljs');
    };

    // one chapter at a time; each leaf's files stand as a rail at the right edge and as an editor's tab bar at the panel's head;
    // a tab opens its file beside the words, the dock docks it left as in an editor, and a press on the code docks it too
    const leaves = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.pd-leaf'));
    for (const leaf of leaves) {
        const chapter = leaf.dataset.chapter;
        const listings = Array.from(leaf.querySelectorAll('.pd-listing'));
        const files = listings.map(listing => listing.querySelector('.pd-word').textContent.trim());
        leaf.dataset.panel = 'closed';
        leaf.dataset.numbers = 'on';
        leaf.dataset.wrap = 'off';
        listings.forEach((listing, index) => highlight(listing, files[index]));
        // the rail's hint of what a press opens: a skeleton of the file's own first lines, each bar as long as its line
        const skeleton = (listing) => '<span class="pd-skeleton">' + Array.from(listing.querySelectorAll('.pd-code-line')).slice(0, 14).map(line => '<i style="width:' + Math.max(12, Math.min(100, line.textContent.length * 2.2)) + '%"></i>').join('') + '</span>';
        leaf.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', '<div class="pd-rail">' + files.map((file, index) => '<button class="pd-tab kind-' + kindOf(chapter, file) + '" data-file="' + index + '">' + fileIcon + '<span class="pd-tab-name">' + file + '</span>' + skeleton(listings[index]) + '</button>').join('') + '</div>');
        const paragraphs = Array.from(leaf.querySelectorAll('.pd-words .pd-paragraph')).slice(0, 16);
        leaf.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', '<button class="pd-grip" title="the words"><span class="pd-skeleton">' + paragraphs.map(paragraph => '<i style="width:' + Math.max(25, Math.min(100, paragraph.textContent.length / 4)) + '%"></i>').join('') + '</span></button>');
        leaf.querySelector('.pd-files').insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin',
            '<div class="pd-tabs">' + files.map((file, index) => '<button class="pd-tab kind-' + kindOf(chapter, file) + '" data-file="' + index + '">' + fileIcon + file + '</button>').join('')
            + '<button class="pd-words-only">words</button>'
            + '<button class="pd-dock">full screen</button>'
            + '<span class="pd-options"><button class="pd-option" data-option="code" aria-pressed="false">light</button><button class="pd-option" data-option="wrap" aria-pressed="false">wrap</button><button class="pd-option" data-option="numbers" aria-pressed="true">lines</button></span>'
            + '</div>');
        const presses = files.map((file, index) => { const kind = kindOf(chapter, file); return '<button class="pd-kind-press kind-' + kind + '" data-file="' + index + '" title="' + names[kind] + '">' + fileIcon + file + '</button>'; }).join('');
        (leaf.querySelector('.pd-title').closest('a') ?? leaf.querySelector('.pd-title')).insertAdjacentHTML('afterend', '<div class="pd-kinds">' + presses + '</div>');
        // the chapter's own mark, at the left of its title, as the book's mark stands at the left of its name in the bar
        leaf.querySelector('.pd-title').insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', glyph(chapters[chapter] ?? 'noun'));
        const open = (index, how) => {
            const same = leaf.dataset.file === String(index);
            leaf.dataset.file = String(index);
            listings.forEach((listing, at) => listing.classList.toggle('pa-open', at === index));
            leaf.querySelectorAll('.pd-rail .pd-tab, .pd-tabs .pd-tab, .pd-kind-press').forEach(tab => tab.classList.toggle('pa-open', tab.dataset.file === String(index)));
            leaf.dataset.panel = how ?? (same && leaf.dataset.panel !== 'closed' ? 'closed' : leaf.dataset.panel === 'closed' ? 'open' : leaf.dataset.panel);
            leaf.querySelector('.pd-dock').textContent = leaf.dataset.panel === 'full' ? 'split' : 'full screen';
            syncTree(leaf);
        };
        leaf.querySelectorAll('.pd-rail .pd-tab').forEach(tab => tab.addEventListener('click', () => open(Number(tab.dataset.file))));
        leaf.querySelectorAll('.pd-tabs .pd-tab').forEach(tab => tab.addEventListener('click', () => open(Number(tab.dataset.file), leaf.dataset.panel === 'closed' ? 'open' : leaf.dataset.panel)));
        leaf.querySelectorAll('.pd-kind-press').forEach(press => press.addEventListener('click', () => open(Number(press.dataset.file))));
        leaf.querySelector('.pd-dock').addEventListener('click', () => open(Number(leaf.dataset.file ?? 0), leaf.dataset.panel === 'full' ? 'open' : 'full'));
        leaf.querySelector('.pd-grip').addEventListener('click', () => open(Number(leaf.dataset.file ?? 0), 'open'));
        leaf.querySelector('.pd-words-only').addEventListener('click', () => open(Number(leaf.dataset.file ?? 0), 'closed'));
        listings.forEach((listing, index) => listing.querySelector('.pd-code').addEventListener('click', () => { if (leaf.dataset.panel !== 'full') open(index, 'full'); }));
        for (const option of leaf.querySelectorAll('.pd-option'))
            option.addEventListener('click', () => {
                const pressed = option.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true';
                option.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(pressed));
                if (option.dataset.option === 'code') document.body.dataset.code = pressed ? 'light' : 'dark';
                if (option.dataset.option === 'wrap') leaf.dataset.wrap = pressed ? 'on' : 'off';
                if (option.dataset.option === 'numbers') leaf.dataset.numbers = pressed ? 'on' : 'off';
            });
        leaf.open = open;
        leaf.files = files;
    }

    // the index as a tree: each group a folder that folds; each chapter a page; under a chapter whose leaf is on this page, its files
    // one explorer: a chevron at every folder — each group, and each chapter that has files — and a row for everything
    const twist = (open) => '<span class="pd-twist' + (open ? ' open' : '') + '"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M6 3.5 10.5 8 6 12.5"/></svg></span>';
    const sections = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pd-section'));
    for (const section of sections) {
        const heading = section.querySelector('.pd-heading');
        if (!heading) continue;
        heading.closest('a').insertAdjacentHTML('beforebegin', '<button class="pd-folder">' + twist(true) + folder + '<span>' + heading.textContent + '</span></button>');
        section.querySelector('.pd-folder').addEventListener('click', () => { section.classList.toggle('folded'); section.querySelector('.pd-twist').classList.toggle('open', !section.classList.contains('folded')); });
    }
    for (const row of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pa-entry')) {
        const anchor = row.closest('a');
        const name = (anchor?.getAttribute('href') ?? '').split('#')[1];
        const leaf = leaves.find(one => one.dataset.chapter === name);
        row.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', (leaf ? twist(true) : '<span class="pd-twist"></span>') + (name in chapters ? glyph(chapters[name]) : icons.page));
        if (!leaf) continue;
        anchor.insertAdjacentHTML('afterend', leaf.files.map((file, index) => '<button class="pd-file kind-' + kindOf(name, file) + '" data-chapter="' + name + '" data-file="' + index + '">' + fileIcon + file + '</button>').join(''));
        row.querySelector('.pd-twist').addEventListener('click', event => {
            event.preventDefault();
            event.stopPropagation();
            const open = !row.querySelector('.pd-twist').classList.contains('open');
            row.querySelector('.pd-twist').classList.toggle('open', open);
            for (const file of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pd-file[data-chapter="' + name + '"]')) file.hidden = !open;
        });
    }
    for (const file of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pd-file'))
        file.addEventListener('click', () => { show(file.dataset.chapter); leaves.find(one => one.dataset.chapter === file.dataset.chapter).open(Number(file.dataset.file), 'open'); });
    // the key, folded at the foot of the tree
    document.querySelector('.pd-holds .pd-chapter').insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', '<div class="pd-section pd-key-section folded"><button class="pd-folder">' + twist(false) + folder + '<span>Key</span></button>' + Object.keys(glyphs).map(kind => '<div class="pd-key">' + glyph(kind) + names[kind] + '</div>').join('') + '</div>');
    const key = document.querySelector('.pd-key-section');
    key.querySelector('.pd-folder').addEventListener('click', () => { key.classList.toggle('folded'); key.querySelector('.pd-twist').classList.toggle('open', !key.classList.contains('folded')); });

    const syncTree = (leaf) => {
        for (const file of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pd-file'))
            file.classList.toggle('pa-open', file.dataset.chapter === leaf.dataset.chapter && file.dataset.file === leaf.dataset.file && leaf.dataset.panel !== 'closed');
    };
    const show = (name) => {
        for (const leaf of leaves) leaf.hidden = leaf.dataset.chapter !== name;
        for (const row of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds .pa-entry')) row.classList.toggle('pa-open', (row.closest('a')?.getAttribute('href') ?? '').endsWith('#' + name));
        const leaf = leaves.find(one => one.dataset.chapter === name);
        if (leaf) syncTree(leaf);
        window.scrollTo({ top: 0 });
    };
    const first = leaves.find(leaf => !leaf.hidden)?.dataset.chapter ?? leaves[0].dataset.chapter;
    show(location.hash && leaves.some(leaf => leaf.dataset.chapter === location.hash.slice(1)) ? location.hash.slice(1) : first);
    for (const anchor of document.querySelectorAll('.pd-holds a[href*="#"]'))
        anchor.addEventListener('click', event => {
            const name = anchor.getAttribute('href').split('#')[1];
            if (!leaves.some(leaf => leaf.dataset.chapter === name)) return;
            event.preventDefault();
            history.replaceState(null, '', '#' + name);
            show(name);
        });

</script>
</body>
</html>
The Paragraphs
What a paragraph may be
Most of this book is ordinary paragraphs. Five sorts are not. One is a question I am asked. One is what I said, in my own words. One is a design I chose. One is a pain a person met using what was built. One is what I think solves it.
A paragraph says which of these it is. So a page can show a question and its answer differently, and everything I said can be found. The questions and my answers are in What I Am Asked, the designs I chose are in The Designs I Am Going With, and the pains and their solutions are in Driving the Build.
code.tsx

The Concept
What a concept is
A concept is one sketch of one idea. In Every Concept each has a section of its own: its name, its number, what it is drawn after, the idea in a sentence, a photograph of it at a desk and on a phone, what I said of it if I said anything, and last the sketch's own code.
The section says it is a concept and gives its number, which it keeps for good. I answer by that number. The sketch itself is a file kept beside the chapter. It is there to document the concept, so its section prints it as code, and nothing in this library opens it or draws it.
Another chapter points to a concept by its number, as a link to its place in Every Concept. It does not show the concept a second time.
The number is drawn where the section says it is a concept, as the note of that saying, so it stands on the card before the name. A concept opened across the screen has a close, a word written in its section as a link back to Every Concept, which the gallery shows only then.
code.tsx
import { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { $, $check, selection } from '@dna-platform/chemistry';
import { $Annotation, $Paragraph, $Section, $Writing, AnnotationSpecification, html, specify } from '@dna-platform/public';

export class $Concept extends $Annotation {
    specification = new ConceptSpecification();
    span = selection.span.attrs({ className: 'pa-number' })``;
    get number(): number {
        const written = html.copy(this.text).trim();
        return written === '' ? NaN : Number(written);
    }

    override note(): ReactNode {
        const Span = this.span;
        return <Span>{this.number}</Span>;
    }

    override defines(writing: $Writing): void {
        writing.classes.add(this, 'pa-concept');
        if ((writing as $Section).mention?.identifier === this.book?.$bookmark) writing.classes.add(this, 'pa-open');
    }

    override erase(writing: $Writing): void {
        writing.classes.revert(this);
    }
}

export class $Photographs extends $Annotation {
    specification = new OfAConceptSpecification();

    override defines(writing: $Writing): void {
        writing.classes.add(this, 'pa-photographs');
    }

    override erase(writing: $Writing): void {
        writing.classes.revert(this);
    }
}

export class $Source extends $Annotation {
    specification = new OfAConceptSpecification();

    override defines(writing: $Writing): void {
        writing.classes.add(this, 'pa-source');
    }

    override erase(writing: $Writing): void {
        writing.classes.revert(this);
    }
}

export class $Close extends $Annotation {
    specification = new OfAConceptSpecification();

    override defines(writing: $Writing): void {
        writing.classes.add(this, 'pa-close');
    }

    override erase(writing: $Writing): void {
        writing.classes.revert(this);
    }
}

export class ConceptSpecification extends AnnotationSpecification {
    @specify('a concept is said of a section')
    $saidOfASection(writing: $Writing): void {
        $check(writing instanceof $Section, 'a concept is said of a section, and this is not one');
    }

    @specify('a concept is given its number')
    $givenItsNumber(writing: $Writing): void {
        $check(Number.isInteger(writing.annotations.expressed($Concept)?.number),
            'a concept is given its number, and this one was given something else');
    }
}

export class OfAConceptSpecification extends AnnotationSpecification {
    @specify('this is said of a paragraph of a concept')
    $saidOfAParagraphOfAConcept(writing: $Writing): void {
        $check(writing instanceof $Paragraph && writing.parent instanceof $Writing && writing.parent.is($Concept),
            'this is said of a paragraph of a concept, and here it is said of something else');
    }
}

export const Concept = $($Concept);
export const Photographs = $($Photographs);
export const Source = $($Source);
export const Close = $($Close);
The Camera
What the camera is
A concept is a page, and this book shows a photograph of it at a desk's width and another at a phone's. The camera takes those photographs. It is the one tool this book needs that the framework does not give, so it is kept here, beside the chapter that says what it is, and nothing that builds this book is kept outside it. It was once a script kept outside the library, and how it came to be here is told in Closure.
It looks at every concept that is kept beside a chapter of this book under its number, photographs the ones that are newer than their photographs, and says how many things on each run past the right edge of the screen. That count is how a page that does not fit a phone is caught before I am shown it. It writes nothing but the photographs, and the book is bound afterwards in the usual way.
The camera photographs concepts. A page of the library itself is looked at with the workbench, which keeps the page open while I write it.
camera.mjs
// Photographs each concept of this book that is newer than its photographs, at a desk's width and at a phone's,
// and says what on it runs past the edge of the screen. Run from anywhere:
//
//     node .me/.design/o3-the-camera~camera.mjs
//
// A concept is a page kept beside a chapter under its number, as 3-every-concept~025.html. Its two
// photographs are kept beside it under the same number. Bind the book afterwards.
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { existsSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const book = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const require = createRequire(join(book, '../../package.json'));
const devices = [
    { name: 'desk', width: 1280, height: 800 },
    { name: 'phone', width: 390, height: 844 },
];

const older = (photograph, concept) => !existsSync(photograph) || statSync(photograph).mtimeMs < statSync(concept).mtimeMs;
const concepts = readdirSync(book).filter(file => /~\d{3}\.html$/u.test(file)).sort();
const wanted = concepts.flatMap(file => devices.map(device => ({ file, device, photograph: join(book, file.replace(/\.html$/u, `-${device.name}.png`)) })))
    .filter(shot => older(shot.photograph, join(book, shot.file)));

if (wanted.length === 0) console.log(`${concepts.length} concepts, every photograph current`);
else {
    const puppeteer = require('puppeteer');
    const browser = await puppeteer.launch({ headless: true, ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--hide-scrollbars'] });
    for (const shot of wanted) {
        const page = await browser.newPage();
        await page.setViewport({ width: shot.device.width, height: shot.device.height, deviceScaleFactor: 1 });
        await page.goto(pathToFileURL(join(book, shot.file)).href, { waitUntil: 'networkidle0' });
        await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
        await new Promise(done => setTimeout(done, 500));
        const past = await page.evaluate(() => {
            const wide = document.documentElement.clientWidth;
            return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('body *')).filter(one => {
                const box = one.getBoundingClientRect();
                return box.width > 0 && box.right > wide + 1 && getComputedStyle(one).position !== 'fixed';
            }).length;
        });
        await page.screenshot({ path: shot.photograph });
        await page.close();
        console.log(`${shot.file} at a ${shot.device.name}: photographed, ${past} past the right edge`);
    }
    await browser.close();
    console.log(`photographed ${wanted.length}; bind the book to see them`);
}
The Gallery
The concepts as cards
A gallery is said of a chapter whose sections are concepts. In it, each group of concepts is a grid, and each concept is a card: its two photographs first, then its name, what it is after, its idea, and what I said of it. The sketch's own code is not on the card.
A card opens across the whole gallery when its address is the one I am at, and then it shows its photographs at full size and the sketch's code under them. The concept says of itself that it is open when the book's bookmark names it, and the gallery reads that; no card keeps a state of its own.
The two paragraphs the card places are said to be what they are in the chapter: the one holding the photographs is the pictures, and the one holding the code is the source. Both are sorts of a concept's paragraph.
code.tsx
import { $, $check, selection } from '@dna-platform/chemistry';
import { $Chapter, $Format, $Writing, AnnotationSpecification, specify } from '@dna-platform/public';

export class $Gallery extends $Format {
    specification = new GallerySpecification();
    themeProvider = true;
    style = selection.div`
        .pd-chapter.pa-gallery .pd-section {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(${({ theme }) => theme.card}, 1fr));
            gap: ${({ theme }) => theme.space};
            align-items: start;
        }
        .pa-gallery .pd-section .pa-self-reference.pd-container, .pa-gallery .pd-section .pd-paragraph { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
        .pa-gallery .pd-section.pa-concept {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr);
            grid-template-areas: 'pictures pictures' 'number name';
            align-items: baseline;
            gap: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} / 2);
        }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pa-number { grid-area: number; }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pa-self-reference.pd-container { grid-area: name; }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pd-paragraph { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pd-paragraph.pa-photographs {
            grid-area: pictures;
            display: flex;
            gap: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} / 2);
            overflow: hidden;
        }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pa-photographs img { height: ${({ theme }) => theme.photo}; width: auto; max-width: none; }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pd-paragraph.pa-source, .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pd-paragraph.pa-close { display: none; }
        .pa-gallery .pd-section.pa-concept.pa-open {
            position: fixed;
            inset: 0 0 0 ${({ theme }) => theme.holdsColumn};
            z-index: 1;
            overflow-y: auto;
            padding: ${({ theme }) => theme.space} calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} * 1.17);
            background: ${({ theme }) => theme.paper};
            grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto;
            grid-template-areas: 'number name close' 'pictures pictures pictures';
            align-content: start;
        }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept.pa-open .pd-paragraph.pa-close {
            display: block;
            grid-area: close;
            margin: 0;
            font-size: calc(1.6 * ${({ theme }) => theme.size});
            line-height: 1;
        }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept.pa-open .pa-close .pa-reference { text-decoration: none; }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept.pa-open .pd-paragraph.pa-photographs, .pa-gallery .pa-concept.pa-open .pd-paragraph.pa-source { max-width: none; }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept.pa-open .pa-photographs { flex-wrap: wrap; overflow: visible; }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept.pa-open .pa-photographs img { height: auto; max-width: 100%; }
        @media (max-width: ${({ theme }) => theme.narrow}) {
            .pa-gallery .pd-section.pa-concept.pa-open { inset: ${({ theme }) => theme.barHeight} 0 0 0; }
        }
        .pa-gallery .pa-concept.pa-open .pd-paragraph.pa-source { display: block; }
        @media (max-width: ${({ theme }) => theme.narrow}) {
            .pa-gallery .pd-section.pa-concept.pa-open { inset: 0; }
        }
    `;

    override defines(writing: $Writing): void {
        super.defines(writing);
        writing.classes.add(this, 'pa-gallery');
    }

    override erase(writing: $Writing): void {
        super.erase(writing);
        writing.classes.revert(this);
    }
}

export class GallerySpecification extends AnnotationSpecification {
    @specify('a gallery is said of a chapter')
    $saidOfAChapter(writing: $Writing): void {
        $check(writing instanceof $Chapter, 'a gallery is said of a chapter, and this is not one');
    }
}

export const Gallery = $($Gallery);
The Frame
How this book is laid out
This book stands in the frame every book of mine stands in, drawn by the base book: the library's bar across the top with the library's subjects and me, this book's contents down the side, its name and its switches at the head, and the page beside. It wears the frame in the light tone, white, which is this book's colour, and offers its two tones as tabs at its head — white, and the black side bar, two of the three tones — because this is the book I look at them in. The six arrangements it once offered as tabs are gone: an arrangement is a book's, fixed where the book is registered, and every book of mine wears the same one. Its own colour, the rose the frame's sketch gives it, is on its index and its pressed tabs.
The design it follows is the white top bar and the opal side bar in the light tone, with the white cards in its gallery; the black side bar is its other option, one tab away, and the blue with the black top is sketched before it is a tab.
The class of this book overrides what the base draws in two places only: which chapter opens when none is named, the gallery, and its switches. Its theme sets its colour and adds the look of the cards and the words. Its cover and its table of contents are the framework's own.
code.tsx
import { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { $ } from '@dna-platform/chemistry';
import { $Chapter, Theme } from '@dna-platform/public';
import { $LibraryBook, Dark as dark, Light as light, Tab as tab, Tone as tone } from '../.manual/.book';
import { Gallery } from './o4-the-gallery~code.tsx';
import { DesignTheme } from './o5-the-frame~theme.tsx';

export class $Design extends $LibraryBook {
    get gallery(): $Chapter | undefined {
        return this.chapters.find(chapter => chapter.is(Gallery));
    }
    override get open(): $Chapter | undefined {
        return super.open ?? this.gallery;
    }

    override switches(): ReactNode {
        const Tab = $(tab);
        return (
            <>
                <Tab
                    chapter={this.cover}
                    of={dark}
                    among={this.tones}
                >
                    cobalt
                </Tab>
                <Tab
                    chapter={this.cover}
                    of={light}
                    among={this.tones}
                >
                    white
                </Tab>
            </>
        );
    }
}

export const Design = $($Design);
$(Design, Theme)(DesignTheme);
$(Design, tone)(dark);
theme.tsx
import { css, RuleSet } from 'styled-components';
import { $ } from '@dna-platform/chemistry';
import { $LibraryBookTheme } from '../.manual/.book';

export class $DesignTheme extends $LibraryBookTheme {
    colour = '#3b6cf0';
    accent = '#1f4fd6';
    bar = '#1f4fd6';
    barInk = '#ffffff';
    barDim = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.74)';
    barOn = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.16)';
    barLine = '#1a44b8';
    mark = '#ffffff';
    side = '#ffffff';
    sideOn = '#e6eeff';
    sideLine = '#e4e8f3';
    ink = '#111318';
    heading = '#111318';
    serif = "'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif";

    protected override parts(): RuleSet[] {
        return [...super.parts(), this.tools(), this.words(), this.cards(), this.small()];
    }

    protected tools(): RuleSet {
        return css`
            .pd-head { border-block-end: thin solid ${({ theme }) => theme.line}; }
            .pd-head .pd-switch {
                border: none;
                border-radius: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} * 0.375);
                padding: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} / 4) calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} / 2);
                background: ${({ theme }) => theme.panel};
                color: ${({ theme }) => theme.soft};
            }
        `;
    }

    protected words(): RuleSet {
        return css`
            .pd-pages { padding: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} * 0.83) calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} * 1.17) calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} * 1.67); }
            .pd-words .pd-chapter { margin-block: 0; max-width: none; }
            .pd-head .pd-title {
                font-size: calc(2 * ${({ theme }) => theme.size});
                letter-spacing: -0.02em;
            }
            .pd-words .pd-title {
                font-family: ${({ theme }) => theme.serif};
                font-size: calc(2 * ${({ theme }) => theme.size});
                font-weight: 600;
                letter-spacing: -0.02em;
                line-height: 1.1;
                color: ${({ theme }) => theme.heading};
            }
            .pd-words .pd-heading {
                font-size: calc(0.76 * ${({ theme }) => theme.size});
                font-weight: 600;
                letter-spacing: 0.12em;
                text-transform: uppercase;
                color: ${({ theme }) => theme.soft};
            }
            .pd-words .pd-paragraph { max-width: ${({ theme }) => theme.measure}; }
            .pd-front .pd-words .pd-paragraph {
                font-size: calc(1.14 * ${({ theme }) => theme.size});
                line-height: 1.6;
                color: ${({ theme }) => theme.soft};
            }
        `;
    }

    protected cards(): RuleSet {
        return css`
            .pa-gallery .pd-section.pa-concept {
                padding: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} * 0.6);
                border: thin solid ${({ theme }) => theme.line};
                border-radius: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} * 0.6);
                background: ${({ theme }) => theme.paper};
                box-shadow: ${({ theme }) => theme.shadow};
            }
            .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pd-heading, .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pa-number {
                font-family: ${({ theme }) => theme.serif};
                font-size: calc(1.07 * ${({ theme }) => theme.size});
                font-weight: 600;
                letter-spacing: -0.01em;
                text-transform: none;
                color: ${({ theme }) => theme.heading};
            }
            .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pa-number {
                font-size: calc(1.07 * ${({ theme }) => theme.size});
                color: ${({ theme }) => theme.soft};
            }
            .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pd-paragraph {
                margin-block: 0;
                font-size: calc(0.86 * ${({ theme }) => theme.size});
                color: ${({ theme }) => theme.soft};
            }
            .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pd-paragraph.pa-answer {
                padding-inline-start: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} / 2);
                border-inline-start: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} / 8) solid ${({ theme }) => theme.me};
                color: ${({ theme }) => theme.ink};
            }
            .pa-gallery .pa-concept .pa-photographs img { border-radius: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} / 4); border: thin solid ${({ theme }) => theme.line}; }
            .pa-gallery .pa-concept.pa-open { box-shadow: 0 0 0 calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} / 8) ${({ theme }) => theme.accent}; }
        `;
    }

    protected small(): RuleSet {
        return css`
            @media (max-width: ${({ theme }) => theme.narrow}) {
                .pd-holds, .pd-library { border-inline-end: none; }
                .pd-pages { padding: calc(${({ theme }) => theme.space} * 0.67); }
            }
        `;
    }
}

export const DesignTheme = $($DesignTheme);
faces.tsx
import { $ } from '@dna-platform/chemistry';
import { $BookshelfCover } from '../.manual/.book';

export { TableOfContents } from '@dna-platform/public';

export class $DesignCover extends $BookshelfCover { }

export const Cover = $($DesignCover);
The Print
A design is drawn on the book's own words
In the design phase I do not sketch a page; I design the page itself. The tool beside this chapter takes a book's print — the page the binder wrote, exactly as the site serves it — and makes a design page from it: the bar, me, the table of contents, the front and every chapter's page, hidden, with the framework's class names kept on every element and nothing else. The page gets a style of its own in place of the printed sheet, and I open it from the file in a browser. Because every element wears the name the live book wears, every rule written on the page can be carried into the book's theme as it is, and because every word is the book's, nothing on the page is pretend.
A page that exists keeps its style and its script; the tool refreshes only the print between them, so after a bind the words on a design page are the book's words again. The first page made this way is The Bookshelf; its own additions — the desk, the marks, the two states — are written in its script and stand on the print's names. The method as a whole, for anyone designing a book of this library, is the branch library's chapter beside the framework, Designing a Page from Its Print; the photographs come later, from the camera.
print.mjs
// Makes a design page from a book's print, so a design is drawn on the book's own words. Run from the repository:
//
//     node .me/.design/o6-the-print~print.mjs dougs-library .me/.design/6-the-story~035.html
//
// The first argument is the book's folder in the last bind, .me/..public/<book>/; the second is the page to write,
// beside the chapter that designs it. The page holds what the print holds — the bar, me, the table of contents, the front
// and every page, hidden — with the framework's class names kept and the styled components' hashes dropped, so every
// rule the page needs can be written against the names the live book wears. A page that already exists keeps its
// <style> and its <script>: only the print between them is refreshed. Bind first; the print is read, never the source.
import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const [book, page] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!book || !page) { console.log('usage: node o6-the-print~print.mjs <book folder> <page to write>'); process.exit(1); }
const library = dirname(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)));
const print = join(library, '..public', book, 'index.html');
if (!existsSync(print)) { console.log(`no print at ${print} — bind first`); process.exit(1); }
const html = readFileSync(print, 'utf8');

const start = html.indexOf('<div id="root">');
const root = html.slice(start, html.indexOf('<script', start));
// the framework's names stay; a styled component's hash goes
const clean = (markup) => markup
    .replace(/ class="([^"]*)"/gu, (m, c) => { const kept = c.split(' ').filter(x => /^p[ad]-/u.test(x)); return kept.length ? ` class="${kept.join(' ')}"` : ''; })
    .replace(/<!--\$-->|<!--\/\$-->/gu, '');
// one element, balanced, from its opening tag
const balanced = (at) => {
    let depth = 0;
    const tag = /<\/?div\b[^>]*>/gu; tag.lastIndex = at;
    for (let m; (m = tag.exec(root));) { depth += m[0].startsWith('</') ? -1 : 1; if (depth === 0) return root.slice(at, m.index + m[0].length); }
    return '';
};
const region = (cls) => { const at = root.indexOf(`<div class="${cls}">`); return at < 0 ? '' : clean(balanced(at)); };
const pages = [];
for (let at = root.indexOf('<div class="pd-page'); at >= 0; at = root.indexOf('<div class="pd-page', at + 1)) {
    const page = balanced(at);
    if (page.startsWith('<div class="pd-page pd-front')) continue;
    const id = page.match(/<div id="([^"]+)" class="pd-sentence pd-title/u)?.[1] ?? `page-${pages.length + 1}`;
    pages.push(clean(page).replace(/^<div class="pd-page[^"]*"/u, `<div class="pd-page" data-chapter="${id}" hidden`));
}
const regions = {
    library: region('pd-library'),
    me: region('pd-me'),
    holds: region('pd-holds'),
    front: region('pd-page pd-front pd-open'),
};
const printed = `${regions.library}\n${regions.me}\n${regions.holds}\n<div class="pd-pages">\n<section class="pd-desk"></section>\n${regions.front}\n${pages.join('\n')}\n</div>`;

const name = basename(page).replace(/~\d+\.html$/u, '').replace(/^\d+-/u, '').split('-').map(word => word[0].toUpperCase() + word.slice(1)).join(' ');
const number = basename(page).match(/~(\d+)\.html$/u)?.[1] ?? '';
let style = `<style>\n    /* the page's own style, written against the print's names */\n</style>`;
let script = '';
let head = `<title>${name}</title>\n<meta name="number" content="${number}">\n<meta name="state" content="design">\n<meta name="after" content="">\n<meta name="idea" content="">\n<meta name="said" content="">`;
if (existsSync(page)) {
    const existing = readFileSync(page, 'utf8');
    style = existing.match(/<style>[\s\S]*?<\/style>/u)?.[0] ?? style;
    script = existing.match(/<script>[\s\S]*?<\/script>/u)?.[0] ?? '';
    head = existing.match(/<title>[\s\S]*?<meta name="said"[^>]*>/u)?.[0] ?? head;
}
const fonts = `<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com"><link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>\n<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&family=Source+Serif+4:ital,opsz,wght@0,8..60,400;0,8..60,600;0,8..60,700;1,8..60,400&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">`;
const written = `<!doctype html>\n<html lang="en">\n<head>\n<meta charset="utf-8">\n<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">\n${head}\n${fonts}\n${style}\n</head>\n<body>\n<!-- the print of ${book}, as bound; refreshed by o6-the-print~print.mjs -->\n${printed}\n${script}\n</body>\n</html>\n`;
writeFileSync(page, written);
console.log(`${page}: the print of ${book} — ${Object.values(regions).filter(Boolean).length} regions, ${pages.length} pages hidden${script ? ', the page\'s style and script kept' : ''}`);
